627: ```
628: 
629: Fragments produce no wrapper element in the DOM. They are the solution for list items, table rows, and other cases where an extra `<div>` wrapper would be semantically incorrect.
630: 
631: #### Comments
632: 
633: Template comments use `{/* ... */}` syntax (like JSX). These are compile-time only — they do not appear in the rendered HTML:
634: 
635: ```kotlin
636: ---
637: 
638: <div>
639:     {/* This is a template comment — not rendered to HTML */}
640:     <h1>{ props.title }</h1>
641: 
642:     {/* TODO: Replace with actual user data */}
643:     <p>Placeholder content</p>
644: </div>
645: ```
646: 
647: HTML comments `<!-- -->` are also permitted and ARE rendered to the client HTML. Use `{/* */}` for development notes; use `<!-- -->` when you genuinely want HTML comments in output.
648: 
649: ### The `.akt` File Compilation
650: 
651: When the KorE compiler encounters a `.akt` file, it performs a multi-phase compilation distinct from normal `.kore` file compilation:
652: 
653: **Phase 1: File splitting.** The compiler scans for the `---` separator. Everything above is the logic section; everything below is the template section. If no `---` is found, the file is rejected with a compile error: `Missing template separator (---) in .akt file`.
654: 
655: **Phase 2: Logic section parsing.** The logic section is parsed as normal KorE code. Imports are resolved. Props types, state types, and function declarations are type-checked. The declared event handlers are collected with their signatures.
656: 
657: **Phase 3: Template parsing.** The template section is parsed by the aKt template parser, producing a `TemplateAST`. The template parser is an extension of the KorE expression parser: it handles HTML element nodes, component invocation nodes, slot nodes, and embedded `{ }` expression nodes.
658: 
659: **Phase 4: Template type checking.** The template AST is type-checked against the logic section's declarations. Specifically:
660: - Every `{ expr }` node: the expression is type-checked as a KorE expression in a scope that includes `props`, `state`, and all functions declared in the logic section. The expression must evaluate to a renderable type (`String`, `Int`, `AktNode`, `List<AktNode>`, or `null`).
661: - Every `<ComponentName>` invocation: the component's `props` type is resolved. Each attribute is type-checked against the corresponding prop declaration. Required props without defaults that are not provided are compile errors.
662: - Every `onClick={handler}` binding: the handler must match one of the allowed event handler signatures for the event type.
663: 
664: **Phase 5: Static/dynamic split.** The compiler walks the template AST and marks every node as either static (contains no expressions that depend on `props` or `state`) or dynamic (contains at least one such expression). Static subtrees are compiled as binary string constants. This is the basis of the diff protocol optimization.
665: 
666: **Phase 6: Code generation.** The compiler emits Erlang Abstract Format for the component. For a stateful component (`@LiveComponent`), this includes:
667: - A GenServer module implementing the OTP `gen_server` behavior
668: - A `render/1` function that takes the current state and produces a `Rendered` data structure (a tree of static and dynamic parts)
669: - A `handle_event/3` function that dispatches to the declared event handlers
670: - A `mount/1` function
671: - A `update/2` function (for prop changes)
672: - A `terminate/2` function
673: 
674: **The generated BEAM modules for a component `pages/users/[id]/Profile.akt`:**
675: 
676: ```
677: 'KorE.Pages.Users.Id.Profile'         — the GenServer
678: 'KorE.Pages.Users.Id.Profile.Render'  — the render function module (compiled render tree)
679: 'KorE.Pages.Users.Id.Profile.Props'   — the props type (as a map type)
680: ```
681: 
682: ---
683: 
684: ## 11.3 — The Component Model
685: 
686: ### Stateless Function Components
687: 
688: A stateless component receives props and returns markup. It has no lifecycle, no state, no process. The compiler generates a simple function module, not a GenServer.
689: 
690: Stateless components are declared with `@Component`. By convention, they live in their own `.akt` file, but a single file may contain multiple stateless component declarations using the `component` keyword:
691: 
692: ```kotlin
693: // UserCard.akt
694: 
695: import kore.akt.*
696: import myapp.domain.User
697: 
698: @Component
699: props UserCardProps {
700:     val user: User
701:     val size: AvatarSize = .medium
702:     val showRole: Boolean = false
703:     val onClick: ((User) -> Unit)? = null
704: }
705: 
706: ---
707: 
708: <div
709:     class={"user-card user-card--${props.size.name}"}
710:     role={ if (props.onClick != null) "button" else null }
711:     tabIndex={ if (props.onClick != null) 0 else null }
712:     onClick={ if (props.onClick != null) { _ -> props.onClick!!(props.user) } else null }
713: >
714:     <Avatar
715:         src={props.user.avatarUrl}
716:         alt={props.user.name}
717:         size={props.size}
718:     />
719:     <div class="user-card__info">
720:         <span class="user-card__name">{ props.user.name }</span>
721:         { if (props.showRole) {
722:             <span class="user-card__role">{ props.user.role.displayName }</span>
723:         } }
724:     </div>
725: </div>
726: ```
727: 
728: The generated BEAM module for a stateless component is a single function:
729: 
730: ```erlang
731: %% Generated Erlang Abstract Format (illustrative)
732: -module('KorE.UserCard').
733: -export([render/1]).
734: 
735: render(Props) ->
736:     %% Static/dynamic tree representation
737:     #{static => [...], dynamic => [...], ...}.
738: ```
739: 
740: Stateless components can be nested freely, composed inline, and passed as props. They produce no process overhead.
741: 
742: **Inline component declarations** (multiple components in one file):
743: 
744: ```kotlin
745: // badges.akt — multiple small components in one file
746: 
747: @Component
748: props BadgeProps {
749:     val label: String
750:     val variant: BadgeVariant = .default
751: }
752: 
753: component Badge {
754:     <span class={"badge badge--${props.variant.name}"}>
755:         { props.label }
756:     </span>
757: }
758: 
759: @Component
760: props StatusDotProps {
761:     val online: Boolean
762: }
763: 
764: component StatusDot {
765:     <span
766:         class={"status-dot " + if (props.online) "status-dot--online" else "status-dot--offline"}
767:         aria-label={ if (props.online) "Online" else "Offline" }
768:     />
769: }
770: ```
771: 
772: Inline `component` declarations use a block body instead of the `---` separator, since they are embedded within a larger file that may already have a primary template.
773: 
774: ### Stateful Server Components
775: 
776: A stateful component is a GenServer process. Each mounted instance of the component on a connected client has a corresponding process on the server. The process holds the component's state. When state changes, the process re-runs the render function and sends the diff to the client.
777: 
778: Stateful components are declared with `@LiveComponent`:
779: 
780: ```kotlin
781: // LiveSearch.akt
782: 
783: import kore.akt.*
784: import kore.akt.live.*
785: import myapp.services.SearchService
786: 
787: @LiveComponent
788: props LiveSearchProps {
789:     val placeholder: String = "Search..."
790:     val minLength: Int = 2
791:     val onSelect: ((SearchResult) -> Unit)? = null
792: }
793: 
794: data class LiveSearchState(
795:     val query: String = "",
796:     val results: List<SearchResult> = emptyList(),
797:     val loading: Boolean = false,
798:     val selected: SearchResult? = null
799: )
800: 
801: fun mount(props: LiveSearchProps): LiveSearchState =
802:     LiveSearchState()
803: 
804: fun handleQueryChange(event: InputEvent, state: LiveSearchState, props: LiveSearchProps): Pair<LiveSearchState, List<Command>> {
805:     val newQuery = event.value
806:     return if (newQuery.length >= props.minLength) {
807:         Pair(
808:             state.copy(query = newQuery, loading = true, results = emptyList()),
809:             listOf(Command.async("search") { SearchService.search(newQuery) })
810:         )
811:     } else {
812:         Pair(state.copy(query = newQuery, results = emptyList(), loading = false), emptyList())
813:     }
814: }
815: 
816: fun handleSearchResult(results: List<SearchResult>, state: LiveSearchState): LiveSearchState =
817:     state.copy(results = results, loading = false)
818: 
819: fun handleSelect(result: SearchResult, state: LiveSearchState, props: LiveSearchProps): Pair<LiveSearchState, List<Command>> {
820:     val commands = if (props.onSelect != null) {
821:         listOf(Command.callParent(props.onSelect!!, result))
822:     } else emptyList()
823:     return Pair(state.copy(selected = result, query = result.title, results = emptyList()), commands)
824: }
825: 
826: ---
827: 
828: <div class="live-search" role="combobox" aria-expanded={state.results.isNotEmpty()}>
829:     <input
830:         type="text"
831:         value={state.query}
832:         placeholder={props.placeholder}
833:         onChange={handleQueryChange}
834:         aria-autocomplete="list"
835:         aria-controls="search-results"
836:     />
837:     { if (state.loading) {
838:         <div class="live-search__spinner" role="status" aria-label="Searching..." />
839:     } }
840:     { if (state.results.isNotEmpty()) {
841:         <ul id="search-results" class="live-search__results" role="listbox">
842:             {for result in state.results}
843:                 <li
844:                     key={result.id}
845:                     class={"live-search__result" + if (result == state.selected) " live-search__result--selected" else ""}
846:                     role="option"
847:                     aria-selected={result == state.selected}
848:                     onClick={ { _ -> handleSelect(result, state, props) } }
849:                 >
850:                     { result.title }
851:                     { if (result.subtitle != null) {
852:                         <span class="live-search__subtitle">{ result.subtitle }</span>
853:                     } }
854:                 </li>
855:             {/for}
856:         </ul>
857:     } }
858: </div>
859: ```
860: 
861: ### Props System
862: 
863: Props are declared using the `props` keyword followed by a struct name. The struct's fields are the component's props:
864: 
865: ```kotlin
866: props MyComponentProps {
867:     val requiredString: String              // Required, no default
868:     val requiredUser: User                  // Required, complex type
869:     val optionalInt: Int = 0                // Optional with default
870:     val optionalText: String? = null        // Optional nullable
871:     val callback: ((Event) -> Unit)? = null // Optional callback
872: }
873: ```
874: 
875: **Required vs optional**: Props without a default value are required. The compiler verifies at every call site that required props are provided. Props with default values are optional.
876: 
877: **Prop validation at compile time**: The compiler type-checks every prop at every invocation site. Passing a `String` where an `Int` is expected, or omitting a required prop, is a compile error.
878: 
879: **Passing functions as props**: Callbacks are typed as function types. When a stateless component is called from a stateful parent, the callback is a reference to the parent's event handler.
880: 
881: **Spreading props**: The spread operator `...` passes all props from a value to a component invocation:
882: 
883: ```kotlin
884: props ButtonProps {
885:     val label: String
886:     val variant: ButtonVariant = .primary
887:     val disabled: Boolean = false
888:     val onClick: () -> Unit
889: }
890: 
891: ---
892: 
893: // When wrapping a component, spread its props through
894: <div class="button-wrapper">
895:     <Button ...{props} />
896: </div>
897: ```
898: 
899: The spread operator is checked by the compiler: the spread value must be assignment-compatible with the target component's props type. Spreading a type that has fields the target doesn't accept is a compile error unless the target has a `vararg` props declaration (see below).
900: 
901: **Computed prop defaults**: Default values can reference other props using `by`:
902: 
903: ```kotlin
904: props AvatarProps {
905:     val user: User
906:     val alt: String by { props.user.name }  // Computed default
907:     val size: Int = 40
908: }
909: ```
910: 
911: ### Children and Slots
912: 
913: Children are typed as `AktNode` (a single node) or `List<AktNode>` (multiple children). The `children` binding is automatically available in the template:
914: 
915: ```kotlin
916: props PanelProps {
917:     val title: String
918:     val collapsible: Boolean = false
919: }
920: 
921: data class PanelState(val collapsed: Boolean = false)
922: 
923: fun mount(props: PanelProps): PanelState = PanelState()
924: fun handleToggle(state: PanelState): PanelState = state.copy(collapsed = !state.collapsed)
925: 
926: ---
927: 
928: <div class={"panel" + if (state.collapsed) " panel--collapsed" else ""}>
929:     <div class="panel__header">
930:         <h3>{ props.title }</h3>
931:         { if (props.collapsible) {
932:             <button
933:                 onClick={handleToggle}
934:                 aria-expanded={!state.collapsed}
935:                 aria-label={ if (state.collapsed) "Expand panel" else "Collapse panel" }
936:             >
937:                 { if (state.collapsed) "▶" else "▼" }
938:             </button>
939:         } }
940:     </div>
941:     { if (!state.collapsed) {
942:         <div class="panel__body">{ children }</div>
943:     } }
944: </div>
945: ```
946: 
947: Named slots:
948: 
949: ```kotlin
950: // AppLayout.akt
951: 
952: ---
953: 
954: <div class="app-layout">
955:     <nav class="app-layout__nav">
956:         { slot("nav") ?: <DefaultNav /> }
957:     </nav>
958:     <main class="app-layout__main">
959:         { children }
960:     </main>
961:     <footer class="app-layout__footer">
962:         { slot("footer") ?: <DefaultFooter /> }
963:     </footer>
964: </div>
965: ```
966: 
967: Usage:
968: 
969: ```kotlin
970: ---
971: 
972: <AppLayout>
973:     <slot name="nav">
974:         <CustomNav currentUser={state.user} />
975:     </slot>
976: 
977:     <ArticlePage article={state.article} />
978: 
979:     <slot name="footer">
980:         <ArticleFooter author={state.article.author} />
981:     </slot>
982: </AppLayout>
983: ```
984: 
985: ### Component Composition
986: 
987: Stateless components compose by nesting: the outer component's render function evaluates the inner component's render function and splices in the result.
988: 
989: Stateful components compose differently. A `@LiveComponent` embedded inside another `@LiveComponent`'s template creates a child process. The parent process does not directly call the child's render function — it sends the child's props to the child process, which runs its own render cycle and sends its own diffs to the client. The diffs are merged by the client runtime.
990: 
991: This means stateful component composition is **process composition**: each stateful component in the tree is an independent GenServer. Communication between parent and child uses commands:
992: 
993: ```kotlin
994: // Parent to child: via props (normal)
995: <ChildComponent value={state.someValue} />
996: 
997: // Child to parent: via callback prop
998: fun handleChildEvent(result: ChildResult, state: ParentState): ParentState =
999:     state.copy(childResult = result)
1000: 
1001: // In template:
1002: <ChildComponent onResult={handleChildEvent} />
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: For more complex communication, parent and child can communicate via PubSub or via process registry lookup — the same mechanisms any two BEAM processes would use.
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 11.4 — State and Lifecycle
1010: 
1011: aKt's state and lifecycle model is a translation of React's hook model into the BEAM process model. This section maps each React hook to its aKt equivalent precisely.
1012: 
1013: ### `useState` → Component State
1014: 
1015: React:
1016: 
1017: ```tsx
1018: const [count, setCount] = useState(0)
1019: const [user, setUser] = useState<User | null>(null)
1020: 
1021: setCount(prev => prev + 1)
1022: setUser({ name: "Alice" })
1023: ```
1024: 
1025: aKt: State is a single typed value held in the component's GenServer process. There is no `useState` call — state is declared as a `data class`, initialized in `mount`, and updated by returning a new value from event handlers.
1026: 
1027: ```kotlin
1028: // State declaration
1029: data class MyState(
1030:     val count: Int = 0,
1031:     val user: User? = null
1032: )
1033: 
1034: // Initialization (equivalent to useState initial value)
1035: fun mount(props: MyProps): MyState = MyState(count = props.initialCount)
1036: 
1037: // Update (equivalent to setCount / setUser)
1038: fun handleIncrement(state: MyState): MyState =
1039:     state.copy(count = state.count + 1)
1040: 
1041: fun handleSetUser(user: User, state: MyState): MyState =
1042:     state.copy(user = user)
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: The key difference: React state updates are independent per `useState` call. aKt state is a single value — the whole state record is replaced on every update. `data class` with `copy()` provides the ergonomics of partial update. If managing multiple independent pieces of state feels cumbersome, that is a signal to split the component.
1046: 
1047: ### `useEffect` → `mount`, `handle_info`, `terminate`
1048: 
1049: **`useEffect(() => {}, [])` — runs once on mount:**
1050: 
1051: React:
1052: 
1053: ```tsx
1054: useEffect(() => {
1055:     analytics.track("page_view", { page: "dashboard" })
1056:     subscribeToUpdates(userId)
1057: }, [])
1058: ```
1059: 
1060: aKt: `mount` is the equivalent. It runs when the component's process is started (the first render):
1061: 
1062: ```kotlin
1063: fun mount(props: DashboardProps): Pair<DashboardState, List<Command>> {
1064:     return Pair(
1065:         DashboardState(),
1066:         listOf(
1067:             Command.run { Analytics.track(.pageView, mapOf("page" to "dashboard")) },
1068:             Command.subscribe("updates:${props.userId}")
1069:         )
1070:     )
1071: }
1072: ```
1073: 
1074: When `mount` needs to return commands (side effects), it returns `Pair<State, List<Command>>` instead of just `State`. When it needs no side effects, it returns `State` directly.
1075: 
1076: **`useEffect(() => {}, [dep])` — runs when dependency changes:**
1077: 
1078: React:
1079: 
1080: ```tsx
1081: useEffect(() => {
1082:     fetchUserPosts(userId)
1083: }, [userId])
1084: ```
1085: 
1086: aKt: There is no reactive dependency tracking. Instead, this pattern is handled by `update`, which is called when the component's props change:
1087: 
1088: ```kotlin
1089: // 'update' is called when props change — equivalent to useEffect with [dep]
1090: fun update(newProps: PostListProps, oldProps: PostListProps, state: PostListState): Pair<PostListState, List<Command>> {
1091:     return if (newProps.userId != oldProps.userId) {
1092:         Pair(
1093:             state.copy(posts = emptyList(), loading = true),
1094:             listOf(Command.async("fetch_posts") { PostService.getUserPosts(newProps.userId) })
1095:         )
1096:     } else {
1097:         Pair(state, emptyList())
1098:     }
1099: }
1100: ```
1101: 
1102: If the "dependency" is an internal state value (not a prop), the pattern is different: trigger the effect directly from the state transition that changes the value, rather than observing the change reactively.
1103: 
1104: **`useEffect(() => { return cleanup }, [])` — cleanup on unmount:**
1105: 
1106: React:
1107: 
1108: ```tsx
1109: useEffect(() => {
1110:     const sub = subscribeToUpdates(userId)
1111:     return () => sub.unsubscribe()
1112: }, [])
1113: ```
1114: 
1115: aKt: `terminate` is called when the component's process is stopped (the client disconnects or navigates away):
1116: 
1117: ```kotlin
1118: fun mount(props: FeedProps): Pair<FeedState, List<Command>> =
1119:     Pair(FeedState(), listOf(Command.subscribe("feed:${props.userId}")))
1120: 
1121: fun terminate(state: FeedState, props: FeedProps): Unit {
1122:     // Cleanup runs here — Command.subscribe automatically unsubscribes on terminate
1123:     // Explicit cleanup for custom resources:
1124:     ConnectionPool.release(state.connection)
1125: }
1126: ```
1127: 
1128: `Command.subscribe` handles its own cleanup automatically — the subscription is removed when the process stops. Explicit `terminate` is needed only for resources that require manual cleanup beyond what `Command` lifecycle management handles.
1129: 
1130: ### `useReducer` → Explicit State Machine
1131: 
1132: React:
1133: 
1134: ```tsx
1135: type Action = { type: 'increment' } | { type: 'decrement' } | { type: 'reset' }
1136: 
1137: function reducer(state: CounterState, action: Action): CounterState {
1138:     switch (action.type) {
1139:         case 'increment': return { count: state.count + 1 }
1140:         case 'decrement': return { count: state.count - 1 }
1141:         case 'reset':     return { count: 0 }
1142:     }
1143: }
1144: 
1145: const [state, dispatch] = useReducer(reducer, { count: 0 })
1146: dispatch({ type: 'increment' })
1147: ```
1148: 
1149: aKt: `useReducer` is not needed as a distinct construct. The event handler functions collectively ARE the reducer. Each event handler is a state transition function. The "action type" discrimination is done at the routing level (which function is called) rather than inside a single `when` block.
1150: 
1151: For complex state machines where the reducer pattern is genuinely useful, use a sealed class and a single `reduce` function:
1152: 
1153: ```kotlin
1154: sealed class CounterEvent {
1155:     object Increment : CounterEvent()
1156:     object Decrement : CounterEvent()
1157:     data class Reset(val to: Int = 0) : CounterEvent()
1158:     data class SetStep(val step: Int) : CounterEvent()
1159: }
1160: 
1161: data class CounterState(val count: Int, val step: Int = 1)
1162: 
1163: fun reduce(event: CounterEvent, state: CounterState): CounterState = when (event) {
1164:     is CounterEvent.Increment -> state.copy(count = state.count + state.step)
1165:     is CounterEvent.Decrement -> state.copy(count = state.count - state.step)
1166:     is CounterEvent.Reset     -> state.copy(count = event.to)
1167:     is CounterEvent.SetStep   -> state.copy(step = event.step)
1168: }
1169: 
1170: // Event handlers delegate to the reducer
1171: fun handleIncrement(state: CounterState) = reduce(CounterEvent.Increment, state)
1172: fun handleDecrement(state: CounterState) = reduce(CounterEvent.Decrement, state)
1173: fun handleReset(state: CounterState)     = reduce(CounterEvent.Reset(), state)
1174: ```
1175: 
1176: ### `useContext` → PubSub and Process Registry
1177: 
1178: React:
1179: 
1180: ```tsx
1181: const ThemeContext = createContext<Theme>('light')
1182: 
1183: // Provider
1184: <ThemeContext.Provider value={theme}>
1185:     <App />
1186: </ThemeContext.Provider>
1187: 
1188: // Consumer
1189: const theme = useContext(ThemeContext)
1190: ```
1191: 
1192: aKt: `useContext` has two use cases: passing data down a tree without prop drilling, and accessing "global" application state. Both have BEAM-native equivalents.
1193: 
1194: **For tree-scoped shared data (equivalent to Provider/Consumer):** The recommended pattern is to pass the data as props through the tree. aKt does not have a client-side context API because the rendering model is server-side — there is no in-memory component tree that context can traverse. If prop drilling is painful, consider whether the data should be fetched directly in each component that needs it (components have their own processes; the fetch cost is negligible), or whether it should come through the routing/layout system.
1195: 
1196: **For application-wide global state:** PubSub is the mechanism:
1197: 
1198: ```kotlin
1199: // In mount — subscribe to theme changes
1200: fun mount(props: ThemedComponentProps): Pair<ThemedState, List<Command>> =
1201:     Pair(
1202:         ThemedState(theme = ThemeRegistry.current()),
1203:         listOf(Command.subscribe("theme:changes"))
1204:     )
1205: 
1206: // In handle_info — receive theme change messages
1207: fun handle_info(msg: ThemeChanged, state: ThemedState): ThemedState =
1208:     state.copy(theme = msg.newTheme)
1209: ```
1210: 
1211: **For per-session data (current user, auth token, locale):** These are passed through the router as part of the session context, accessible in `mount`:
1212: 
1213: ```kotlin
1214: fun mount(props: MyProps, session: Session): Pair<MyState, List<Command>> {
1215:     val currentUser = session.get<User>("current_user")
1216:     return Pair(MyState(currentUser = currentUser), emptyList())
1217: }
1218: ```
1219: 
1220: ### `useRef` → JS Hook Handle
1221: 
1222: React:
1223: 
1224: ```tsx
1225: const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)
1226: inputRef.current?.focus()
1227: ```
1228: 
1229: aKt: `useRef` is not directly applicable in the server-rendered model because the server does not have a reference to DOM elements. For cases where you need to imperatively interact with a DOM element, the `use:` directive and JS hooks are the mechanism (covered in Section 11.11).
1230: 
1231: For the common focus-management use case:
1232: 
1233: ```kotlin
1234: ---
1235: 
1236: // Server-side: declare the element with a ref id
1237: <input
1238:     type="text"
1239:     use:focus={state.shouldFocus}  // Triggers focus via JS hook when true
1240:     value={state.value}
1241:     onChange={handleChange}
1242: />
1243: ```
1244: 
1245: For storing mutable server-side references across renders (the other common `useRef` use case), store the value in the component's state record. Unlike in React, storing a value in state that does not affect rendering does not cause performance problems — the compiler's static/dynamic split ensures that state fields unused in the template do not trigger diff work.
1246: 
1247: ### `useMemo` / `useCallback` → Computed Values and Module Functions
1248: 
1249: React:
1250: 
1251: ```tsx
1252: const sortedUsers = useMemo(() =>
1253:     [...users].sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name)),
1254:     [users]
1255: )
1256: 
1257: const handleClick = useCallback((id: string) => {
1258:     dispatch({ type: 'select', id })
1259: }, [dispatch])
1260: ```
1261: 
1262: aKt: `useMemo` is unnecessary. Functions called in the template are pure KorE functions — the compiler can inline them and the BEAM's garbage collector handles the output efficiently. There is no need to memoize to prevent re-renders because there is no Virtual DOM reconciliation; the diff protocol only sends changed dynamic values.
1263: 
1264: ```kotlin
1265: // No useMemo needed — this is called on every render, and that's fine
1266: fun sortedUsers(state: UserListState): List<User> =
1267:     state.users.sortedBy { it.name }
1268: 
1269: ---
1270: 
1271: <ul>
1272:     {for user in sortedUsers(state)}
1273:         <li key={user.id}>{ user.name }</li>
1274:     {/for}
1275: </ul>
1276: ```
1277: 
1278: If the sort is genuinely expensive (thousands of items), store the sorted list in state and update it only when the source list changes:
1279: 
1280: ```kotlin
1281: fun handleUsersLoaded(users: List<User>, state: UserListState): UserListState =
1282:     state.copy(
1283:         users = users,
1284:         sortedUsers = users.sortedBy { it.name }  // Computed once on update
1285:     )
1286: ```
1287: 
1288: `useCallback` is not needed because function references in event handlers are resolved at compile time; they are not closures that need to be stabilized to prevent re-renders.
1289: 
1290: ### `useTransition` → `assign_async` Equivalent
1291: 
1292: React:
1293: 
1294: ```tsx
1295: const [isPending, startTransition] = useTransition()
1296: 
1297: startTransition(() => {
1298:     setTab(nextTab)
1299: })
1300: ```

1302: aKt: Async state updates use the `Command.async` mechanism:
1303: 
1304: ```kotlin
1305: fun handleTabChange(tab: Tab, state: PageState): Pair<PageState, List<Command>> =
1306:     Pair(
1307:         state.copy(activeTab = tab, loading = true),
1308:         listOf(Command.async("load_tab_data") { TabService.loadData(tab) })
1309:     )
1310: 
1311: fun handleTabDataLoaded(result: Ok<TabData>, state: PageState): PageState =
1312:     state.copy(tabData = result.value, loading = false)
1313: 
1314: fun handleTabDataError(result: Err<String>, state: PageState): PageState =
1315:     state.copy(error = result.error, loading = false)
1316: ```
1317: 
1318: The `Command.async` system is covered fully in Section 11.8.
1319: 
1320: ### Complete Lifecycle Diagram
1321: 
1322: ```
1323: Client connects
1324:       │
1325:       ▼
1326:   loadData(params)    ← Page-level data loading (like getServerSideProps)
1327:       │
1328:       ▼
1329:   mount(props)        ← Component process starts, initial state set
1330:       │               ← Side effects via Command list
1331:       ▼
1332:   render(state)       ← Template evaluated, diff tree produced
1333:       │               ← Initial HTML sent to client
1334:       ▼
1335:   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
1336:   │                 Component Running                   │
1337:   │                                                     │
1338:   │  User event → handle_event → new state → render     │
1339:   │  Async result → handle_info → new state → render    │
1340:   │  Props change → update → new state → render         │
1341:   │                                                     │
1342:   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
1343:       │
1344:       ▼
1345:   terminate(state)    ← Client disconnects or navigates
1346:                       ← Cleanup runs here
1347: ```
1348: 
1349: **Complete lifecycle example:**
1350: 
1351: ```kotlin
1352: // RealtimeFeed.akt
1353: 
1354: import kore.akt.*
1355: import kore.akt.live.*
1356: import myapp.services.{PostService, PubSub}
1357: import myapp.domain.{Post, User}
1358: 
1359: @LiveComponent
1360: props RealtimeFeedProps {
1361:     val userId: String
1362:     val initialLimit: Int = 20
1363: }
1364: 
1365: data class FeedState(
1366:     val posts: List<Post> = emptyList(),
1367:     val loading: Boolean = true,
1368:     val error: String? = null,
1369:     val newPostCount: Int = 0,
1370:     val limit: Int = 20
1371: )
1372: 
1373: // LIFECYCLE: mount — equivalent to componentDidMount + initial render
1374: fun mount(props: RealtimeFeedProps): Pair<FeedState, List<Command>> =
1375:     Pair(
1376:         FeedState(limit = props.initialLimit),
1377:         listOf(
1378:             Command.async("load_posts") { PostService.getRecent(props.userId, props.initialLimit) },
1379:             Command.subscribe("feed:${props.userId}")
1380:         )
1381:     )
1382: 
1383: // LIFECYCLE: handle_info — receives async results and PubSub messages
1384: fun handle_info(msg: AsyncResult<"load_posts", List<Post>>, state: FeedState): FeedState =
1385:     when (msg) {
1386:         is Ok -> state.copy(posts = msg.value, loading = false)
1387:         is Err -> state.copy(error = msg.reason.toString(), loading = false)
1388:     }
1389: 
1390: fun handle_info(msg: NewPost, state: FeedState): FeedState =
1391:     state.copy(newPostCount = state.newPostCount + 1)
1392: 
1393: // LIFECYCLE: update — equivalent to componentDidUpdate / useEffect([dep])
1394: fun update(newProps: RealtimeFeedProps, oldProps: RealtimeFeedProps, state: FeedState): Pair<FeedState, List<Command>> =
1395:     if (newProps.userId != oldProps.userId) {
1396:         Pair(
1397:             FeedState(loading = true, limit = newProps.initialLimit),
1398:             listOf(
1399:                 Command.unsubscribe("feed:${oldProps.userId}"),
1400:                 Command.async("load_posts") { PostService.getRecent(newProps.userId, newProps.initialLimit) },
1401:                 Command.subscribe("feed:${newProps.userId}")
1402:             )
1403:         )
1404:     } else {
1405:         Pair(state, emptyList())
1406:     }
1407: 
1408: // LIFECYCLE: terminate — cleanup
1409: fun terminate(state: FeedState, props: RealtimeFeedProps): Unit {
1410:     PostService.recordLastViewed(props.userId, state.posts.firstOrNull()?.id)
1411: }
1412: 
1413: // EVENT HANDLERS
1414: fun handleLoadNew(state: FeedState, props: RealtimeFeedProps): Pair<FeedState, List<Command>> =
1415:     Pair(
1416:         state.copy(loading = true, newPostCount = 0),
1417:         listOf(Command.async("load_posts") { PostService.getRecent(props.userId, state.limit) })
1418:     )
1419: 
1420: fun handleLoadMore(state: FeedState, props: RealtimeFeedProps): Pair<FeedState, List<Command>> {
1421:     val newLimit = state.limit + props.initialLimit
1422:     return Pair(
1423:         state.copy(loading = true, limit = newLimit),
1424:         listOf(Command.async("load_posts") { PostService.getRecent(props.userId, newLimit) })
1425:     )
1426: }
1427: 
1428: ---
1429: 
1430: <div class="feed">
1431:     { if (state.newPostCount > 0) {
1432:         <button class="feed__new-posts-banner" onClick={handleLoadNew}>
1433:             { state.newPostCount } new { if (state.newPostCount == 1) "post" else "posts" } — click to load
1434:         </button>
1435:     } }
1436: 
1437:     { when {
1438:         state.loading && state.posts.isEmpty() -> <FeedSkeleton />
1439:         state.error != null -> (
1440:             <div class="feed__error" role="alert">
1441:                 <p>Failed to load posts: { state.error }</p>
1442:                 <button onClick={handleLoadMore}>Retry</button>
1443:             </div>
1444:         )
1445:         state.posts.isEmpty() -> <EmptyFeed userId={props.userId} />
1446:         else -> (
1447:             <>
1448:                 <ul class="feed__list">
1449:                     {for post in state.posts}
1450:                         <li key={post.id}>
1451:                             <PostCard post={post} />
1452:                         </li>
1453:                     {/for}
1454:                 </ul>
1455:                 <button
1456:                     class="feed__load-more"
1457:                     onClick={handleLoadMore}
1458:                     disabled={state.loading}
1459:                 >
1460:                     { if (state.loading) "Loading..." else "Load more" }
1461:                 </button>
1462:             </>
1463:         )
1464:     } }
1465: </div>
1466: ```

1468: ---
1469: 
1470: ## 11.5 — Event Handling
1471: 
1472: aKt's event model is a round-trip protocol: a user interaction on the client generates a WebSocket message, the server's component process receives it and runs the corresponding handler, the handler returns a new state, the server diffs the new render against the previous render, and the diff is sent to the client to update the DOM.
1473: 
1474: The round trip typically completes in under 50ms on a co-located server. For latency-sensitive interactions, optimistic updates and JS hooks provide client-side immediacy.
1475: 
1476: ### Standard Events
1477: 
1478: All standard DOM events are supported. Each maps to a server-side `handle_event` dispatch:
1479: 
1480: | aKt attribute | DOM event | Handler payload type |
1481: |---|---|---|
1482: | `onClick` | `click` | `ClickEvent` |
1483: | `onChange` | `change` (input, select, textarea) | `ChangeEvent` |
1484: | `onInput` | `input` | `InputEvent` |
1485: | `onSubmit` | `submit` (form) | `SubmitEvent` |
1486: | `onKeyDown` | `keydown` | `KeyboardEvent` |
1487: | `onKeyUp` | `keyup` | `KeyboardEvent` |
1488: | `onKeyPress` | `keypress` (deprecated, included for compatibility) | `KeyboardEvent` |
1489: | `onFocus` | `focus` | `FocusEvent` |
1490: | `onBlur` | `blur` | `FocusEvent` |
1491: | `onMouseEnter` | `mouseenter` | `MouseEvent` |
1492: | `onMouseLeave` | `mouseleave` | `MouseEvent` |
1493: | `onMouseMove` | `mousemove` | `MouseEvent` |
1494: | `onMouseDown` | `mousedown` | `MouseEvent` |
1495: | `onMouseUp` | `mouseup` | `MouseEvent` |
1496: | `onDragStart` | `dragstart` | `DragEvent` |
1497: | `onDrop` | `drop` | `DragEvent` |
1498: | `onScroll` | `scroll` | `ScrollEvent` |
1499: 
1500: **Full round-trip example for `onClick`:**
1501: 
1502: ```kotlin
1503: fun handleAddItem(state: CartState): Pair<CartState, List<Command>> =
1504:     Pair(
1505:         state.copy(items = state.items + CartItem.empty()),
1506:         listOf(Command.run { Analytics.track(.addToCart) })
1507:     )
1508: 
1509: ---
1510: 
1511: <button
1512:     onClick={handleAddItem}
1513:     disabled={state.items.size >= 10}
1514:     aria-label="Add item to cart"
1515: >
1516:     Add Item
1517: </button>
1518: ```
1519: 
1520: What happens when the user clicks:
1521: 1. The aKt JS runtime detects the `click` event on the element
1522: 2. The runtime reads the element's encoded event binding (`data-akt-event-click="handleAddItem"`)
1523: 3. The runtime sends `{"type": "event", "name": "handleAddItem", "payload": {}}` over the WebSocket
1524: 4. The component's GenServer process receives the message, dispatches to `handleAddItem`
1525: 5. `handleAddItem` returns `(newState, [Command.run(…)])`
1526: 6. The GenServer updates its state, executes the command, runs `render(newState)`, diffs against the previous render
1527: 7. The diff `{"0": {"disabled": false}}` (for example) is sent to the client
1528: 8. The aKt JS runtime applies the patch
1529: 
1530: ### Event Payload Types
1531: 
1532: ```kotlin
1533: data class ClickEvent(
1534:     val target: ElementRef,
1535:     val clientX: Int,
1536:     val clientY: Int,
1537:     val button: Int,        // 0 = left, 1 = middle, 2 = right
1538:     val ctrlKey: Boolean,
1539:     val shiftKey: Boolean,
1540:     val altKey: Boolean,
1541:     val metaKey: Boolean
1542: )
1543: 
1544: data class InputEvent(
1545:     val value: String,       // Current value of the input
1546:     val target: ElementRef
1547: )
1548: 
1549: data class ChangeEvent(
1550:     val value: String,       // For text/select
1551:     val checked: Boolean?,   // For checkboxes
1552:     val files: List<FileRef>?, // For file inputs
1553:     val target: ElementRef
1554: )
1555: 
1556: data class KeyboardEvent(
1557:     val key: String,         // "Enter", "Escape", "ArrowUp", etc.
1558:     val code: String,        // "KeyA", "Enter", etc.
1559:     val ctrlKey: Boolean,
1560:     val shiftKey: Boolean,
1561:     val altKey: Boolean,
1562:     val metaKey: Boolean,
1563:     val repeat: Boolean
1564: )
1565: 
1566: data class SubmitEvent(
1567:     val formData: Map<String, String>, // Form field name → value
1568:     val target: ElementRef
1569: )
1570: 
1571: data class FocusEvent(
1572:     val target: ElementRef,
1573:     val relatedTarget: ElementRef?
1574: )
1575: 
1576: data class MouseEvent(
1577:     val clientX: Int,
1578:     val clientY: Int,
1579:     val target: ElementRef
1580: )
1581: 
1582: data class ScrollEvent(
1583:     val scrollTop: Int,
1584:     val scrollLeft: Int,
1585:     val target: ElementRef
1586: )
1587: ```
1588: 
1589: ### Preventing Default Behavior
1590: 
1591: Use the `prevent:` modifier:
1592: 
1593: ```kotlin
1594: ---
1595: 
1596: // Prevent form submission
1597: <form onSubmit={handleSubmit} prevent:submit>
1598:     ...
1599: </form>
1600: 
1601: // Prevent link navigation
1602: <a href="/dashboard" onClick={handleNavClick} prevent:click>
1603:     Dashboard
1604: </a>
1605: ```
1606: 
1607: The `prevent:` modifier is compiled to a client-side instruction: before sending the event to the server, call `event.preventDefault()`. This is necessary because the default browser behavior (form submission, link navigation) would navigate away from the page before the server can respond.
1608: 
1609: You can also return a command from an event handler that tells the client to navigate:
1610: 
1611: ```kotlin
1612: fun handleSubmit(event: SubmitEvent, state: FormState): Pair<FormState, List<Command>> {
1613:     val errors = validate(event.formData)
1614:     return if (errors.isEmpty()) {
1615:         Pair(state, listOf(Command.navigate("/dashboard")))
1616:     } else {
1617:         Pair(state.copy(errors = errors), emptyList())
1618:     }
1619: }
1620: ```
1621: 
1622: ### Debouncing and Throttling
1623: 
1624: The `debounce:` and `throttle:` modifiers delay or throttle event sending:
1625: 
1626: ```kotlin
1627: ---
1628: 
1629: // Debounce: wait 300ms after last keystroke before sending
1630: <input
1631:     type="search"
1632:     value={state.query}
1633:     onInput={handleSearch}
1634:     debounce:input={300}
1635: />
1636: 
1637: // Throttle: send at most once per 200ms
1638: <div
1639:     onMouseMove={handleMouseMove}
1640:     throttle:mousemove={200}
1641: />
1642: ```
1643: 
1644: `debounce:` is implemented client-side by the aKt JS runtime: the runtime holds the event and only sends it after the specified delay with no new events of the same type on the same element. `throttle:` sends the event immediately and then suppresses subsequent events of the same type for the specified duration.
1645: 
1646: ### JS Hooks for Client-Side Behavior
1647: 
1648: For behavior that genuinely cannot be implemented server-side — animation, canvas, third-party JavaScript libraries, clipboard API, browser geolocation — the `use:` directive binds a JS hook to a DOM element:
1649: 
1650: ```kotlin
1651: ---
1652: 
1653: <canvas
1654:     use:Chart
1655:     data-config={Json.encode(chartConfig)}
1656:     width="800"
1657:     height="400"
1658: />
1659: ```
1660: 
1661: JS hooks are registered in the aKt JS runtime configuration. The hook lifecycle:
1662: 
1663: ```javascript
1664: // In your app's JS bundle (e.g., app.js)
1665: import { AktRuntime } from "akt-runtime"
1666: 
1667: AktRuntime.start({
1668:     hooks: {
1669:         Chart: {
1670:             // Called when the element is first added to the DOM
1671:             mounted() {
1672:                 const config = JSON.parse(this.el.dataset.config)
1673:                 this.chart = new Chart(this.el, config)
1674:             },
1675: 
1676:             // Called after the server sends a patch that affects this element
1677:             updated() {
1678:                 const config = JSON.parse(this.el.dataset.config)
1679:                 this.chart.data = config.data
1680:                 this.chart.update()
1681:             },
1682: 
1683:             // Called when the element is removed from the DOM
1684:             destroyed() {
1685:                 this.chart.destroy()
1686:             },
1687: 
1688:             // Called when the server sends a custom event to this hook
1689:             handleEvent(event) {
1690:                 if (event.type === "highlight") {
1691:                     this.chart.highlight(event.dataIndex)
1692:                 }
1693:             }
1694:         }
1695:     }
1696: })
1697: ```
1698: 
1699: The `this` context inside a JS hook provides:
1700: 
1701: - `this.el` — the DOM element
1702: - `this.pushEvent(name, payload)` — sends an event to the server component
1703: - `this.handleEvent(name, callback)` — registers a listener for server-sent events
1704: 
1705: Sending events from hook to server:
1706: 
1707: ```javascript
1708: // In JS hook
1709: this.pushEvent("chart_point_clicked", { dataIndex: point.index, value: point.value })
1710: ```
1711: 
1712: ```kotlin
1713: // In component — receiving the hook event
1714: fun handle_info(msg: HookEvent<"chart_point_clicked">, state: DashboardState): DashboardState =
1715:     state.copy(selectedDataIndex = msg.payload["dataIndex"] as Int)
1716: ```
1717: 
1718: Sending events from server to hook:
1719: 
1720: ```kotlin
1721: fun handleHighlightPoint(index: Int, state: DashboardState): Pair<DashboardState, List<Command>> =
1722:     Pair(
1723:         state.copy(highlightedIndex = index),
1724:         listOf(Command.sendToHook("Chart", "highlight", mapOf("dataIndex" to index)))
1725:     )
1726: ```
1727: 
1728: ### Optimistic Updates
1729: 
1730: For low-latency feedback on user interactions, optimistic updates allow the UI to reflect the expected outcome of an event before the server confirms it:
1731: 
1732: ```kotlin
1733: data class LikeButtonState(
1734:     val liked: Boolean,
1735:     val likeCount: Int,
1736:     val pending: Boolean = false
1737: )
1738: 
1739: fun handleLike(state: LikeButtonState, props: LikeButtonProps): Pair<LikeButtonState, List<Command>> {
1740:     // Optimistic update: immediately reflect the change
1741:     val optimisticState = state.copy(
1742:         liked = !state.liked,
1743:         likeCount = if (state.liked) state.likeCount - 1 else state.likeCount + 1,
1744:         pending = true
1745:     )
1746:     return Pair(
1747:         optimisticState,
1748:         listOf(Command.async("toggle_like") { LikeService.toggle(props.postId) })
1749:     )
1750: }
1751: 
1752: fun handle_info(msg: AsyncResult<"toggle_like", LikeResult>, state: LikeButtonState): LikeButtonState =
1753:     when (msg) {
1754:         is Ok -> state.copy(
1755:             liked = msg.value.liked,
1756:             likeCount = msg.value.count,
1757:             pending = false
1758:         )
1759:         is Err -> state.copy(
1760:             // Revert on error
1761:             liked = !state.liked,
1762:             likeCount = if (state.liked) state.likeCount + 1 else state.likeCount - 1,
1763:             pending = false
1764:         )
1765:     }
1766: ```

1800: fun handleFieldChange(event: InputEvent, state: ContactFormState): ContactFormState {
1801:     val fieldName = event.target.name
1802:     val newValues = when (fieldName) {
1803:         "name"    -> state.values.copy(name = event.value)
1804:         "email"   -> state.values.copy(email = event.value)
1805:         "subject" -> state.values.copy(subject = event.value)
1806:         "message" -> state.values.copy(message = event.value)
1807:         else      -> state.values
1808:     }
1809:     // Clear field error on change
1810:     return state.copy(
1811:         values = newValues,
1812:         errors = state.errors - fieldName
1813:     )
1814: }
1815: 
1816: fun handleBlur(event: FocusEvent, state: ContactFormState): ContactFormState {
1817:     val fieldName = event.target.name
1818:     val error = validateField(fieldName, state.values)
1819:     return if (error != null) {
1820:         state.copy(errors = state.errors + (fieldName to error))
1821:     } else {
1822:         state.copy(errors = state.errors - fieldName)
1823:     }
1824: }
1825: 
1826: fun handleSubmit(event: SubmitEvent, state: ContactFormState, props: ContactFormProps): Pair<ContactFormState, List<Command>> {
1827:     val allErrors = validateAll(state.values)
1828:     return if (allErrors.isNotEmpty()) {
1829:         Pair(state.copy(errors = allErrors), emptyList())
1830:     } else {
1831:         Pair(
1832:             state.copy(submitting = true, serverError = null),
1833:             listOf(Command.async("send_message") { MailService.send(state.values) })
1834:         )
1835:     }
1836: }
1837: 
1838: fun handle_info(msg: AsyncResult<"send_message", Unit>, state: ContactFormState, props: ContactFormProps): Pair<ContactFormState, List<Command>> =
1839:     when (msg) {
1840:         is Ok -> {
1841:             val commands = if (props.onSuccess != null) {
1842:                 listOf(Command.run { props.onSuccess!!() })
1843:             } else emptyList()
1844:             Pair(state.copy(submitted = true, submitting = false), commands)
1845:         }
1846:         is Err -> Pair(state.copy(submitting = false, serverError = "Failed to send message. Please try again."), emptyList())
1847:     }
1848: 
1849: // Validation helpers (in logic section, not rendered)
1850: fun validateField(field: String, values: FormValues): String? = when (field) {
1851:     "name"    -> if (values.name.isBlank()) "Name is required" else null
1852:     "email"   -> if (!values.email.matches(Regex.email)) "Valid email required" else null
1853:     "subject" -> if (values.subject.isBlank()) "Subject is required" else null
1854:     "message" -> if (values.message.length < 10) "Message must be at least 10 characters" else null
1855:     else      -> null
1856: }
1857: 
1858: fun validateAll(values: FormValues): Map<String, String> =
1859:     listOf("name", "email", "subject", "message")
1860:         .mapNotNull { field -> validateField(field, values)?.let { field to it } }
1861:         .toMap()
1862:

1974: ## 11.6 — Server vs Client Components
1975: 
1976: ### The Default: Everything is a Server Component
1977: 
1978: In aKt, the default execution model for every `.akt` component is server-side. The component runs as a GenServer process on the BEAM. No JavaScript is shipped to the browser for the component's logic. The server renders HTML, maintains state, processes events via WebSocket, and sends diffs.
1979: 
1980: This is a stronger default than Next.js server components, which require explicit opt-in (`export async function Page()`). In aKt, you do not opt into being a server component. You opt out.
1981: 
1982: The practical implications:
1983: - Zero JavaScript bundle growth as you add components
1984: - Full access to server resources (database, file system, process registry, PubSub) directly in components without an API layer
1985: - No serialization boundary between component logic and data layer — you call your services directly
1986: - Server-side secrets are never exposed to the client
1987: - Search engine crawlers see fully-rendered HTML
1988: 
1989: ### `use client` — Client-Side Islands
1990: 
1991: When a component genuinely needs to run on the client — because it wraps a third-party JavaScript library, requires browser APIs unavailable server-side, or needs sub-millisecond interaction latency that a round-trip cannot provide — it is declared with `use client`:
1992: 
1993: ```kotlin
1994: // SortableList.akt
1995: use client  // Must be the first non-comment line
1996: 
1997: import akt.client.*
1998: 
1999: props SortableListProps {
2000:     val items: List<SortableItem>

(Showing lines 1301-2000 of 3209. Use offset=2001 to continue.)
</content>
```

2025: 
2026: A `use client` component:
2027: - Is compiled to JavaScript (TypeScript via the aKt-to-TS compiler backend) and included in the browser bundle
2028: - Runs in the browser, not on the server
2029: - Does not have a corresponding GenServer process
2030: - Has its own local state managed in the browser
2031: - Communicates with its parent server component via props and callbacks
2032: 
2033: The `use:Sortable` hook in the example above connects to a JavaScript drag-and-drop library:
2034: 
2035: ```javascript
2036: // In app.js
2037: AktRuntime.start({
2038:     hooks: {
2039:         Sortable: {
2040:             mounted() {
2041:                 this.sortable = new SortableJS(this.el, {
2042:                     onEnd: (event) => {
2043:                         const ids = Array.from(this.el.children).map(el => el.dataset.id)
2044:                         this.pushEvent("reordered", { ids })
2045:                     }
2046:                 })
2047:             },
2048:             destroyed() { this.sortable.destroy() }
2049:         }
2050:     }
2051: })
2052: ```
2053: 
2054: ### The Boundary Rules
2055: 
2056: **Rule 1: Server components can use client components.** A server component's template may include `<SortableList>` even though `SortableList` is a client component. The server renders the island's initial HTML (from the `mount` state), marks it with the island metadata, and the client-side runtime hydrates it.
2057: 
2058: ```kotlin
2059: // Dashboard.akt (server component — no 'use client')
2060: 
2061: ---
2062: 
2063: <div class="dashboard">
2064:     <DashboardStats stats={state.stats} />       // Server component
2065:     <RecentActivity feed={state.feed} />          // Server component
2066:     <SortableList                                  // Client component (island)
2067:         items={state.widgets}
2068:         onReorder={handleWidgetReorder}
2069:     />
2070: </div>
2071: ```
2072: 
2073: **Rule 2: Client components cannot use server components.** A `use client` component's template cannot include server components. If it attempts to, the compiler emits an error: `Server component 'DashboardStats' cannot be used inside client component 'SortableList'. Move 'DashboardStats' to the server component tree or convert it to a client component.`
2074: 
2075: **Rule 3: Props crossing the boundary must be serializable.** The parent server component passes props to the client island via the initial HTML payload. Props must be JSON-serializable: primitives, strings, lists, and maps of primitives. The following types cannot cross the boundary:
2076: - Function references (except callbacks, which are encoded as event names)
2077: - GenServer PIDs
2078: - Opaque Erlang terms
2079: - Types annotated `@NotSerializable`
2080: 
2081: The compiler verifies this at the call site. If `state.connection` (type `DBConnection`) is passed as a prop to a client component, the compiler emits: `Type 'DBConnection' is not serializable and cannot cross the server/client boundary`.
2082: 
2083: Callbacks (functions passed as props to client components) are serialized as opaque event identifiers. When the client component invokes the callback, it sends an event to the server, which dispatches the callback on the server side.
2084: 
2085: **Rule 4: Serializable types include:** `Int`, `Long`, `Float`, `Double`, `Boolean`, `String`, `List<T>` where T is serializable, `Map<String, T>` where T is serializable, `data class` types where all fields are serializable, and types implementing `AktSerializable`.
2086: 
2087: ### Streaming and Suspense
2088: 
2089: aKt supports streaming initial HTML: the server begins sending the page's HTML immediately, with placeholder content for components whose data has not yet loaded, then streams the updates as data arrives.
2090: 
2091: The `suspend` modifier on a component's `loadData` function marks it as async-loading:
2092: 
2093: ```kotlin
2094: // UserProfile.akt
2095: 
2096: @LiveComponent
2097: props UserProfileProps {
2098:     val userId: String
2099: }
2100: 
2101: data class UserProfileState(
2102:     val user: User? = null,
2103:     val posts: List<Post> = emptyList(),
2104:     val loading: Boolean = true
2105: )
2106: 
2107: // loadData runs before mount — used for initial SSR data
2108: // The page HTML is streamed with a placeholder until this resolves
2109: suspend fun loadData(props: UserProfileProps): UserProfileState {
2110:     val user = UserService.getById(props.userId)
2111:     return UserProfileState(user = user, loading = false)
2112: }
2113: 
2114: fun mount(props: UserProfileProps, initialState: UserProfileState): Pair<UserProfileState, List<Command>> =
2115:     Pair(
2116:         initialState,
2117:         listOf(Command.async("load_posts") { PostService.getByUser(props.userId) })
2118:     )
2119: 
2120: fun handle_info(msg: AsyncResult<"load_posts", List<Post>>, state: UserProfileState): UserProfileState =
2121:     state.copy(posts = msg.value)
2122: ```
2123: 
2124: While `loadData` is running, the page renders the corresponding `_loading.akt` template (see Section 11.7). Once `loadData` resolves, the full component renders. This is the server-side equivalent of React Suspense's streaming SSR.
2125: 
2126: **Per-component async loading with `assign_async`:**
2127: 
2128: For data that loads after mount (not blocking initial render), use `Command.async`:
2129: 
2130: ```kotlin
2131: data class ProductPageState(
2132:     val product: Product,
2133:     val relatedProducts: AsyncValue<List<Product>> = AsyncValue.loading(),
2134:     val reviews: AsyncValue<List<Review>> = AsyncValue.loading()
2135: )
2136: 
2137: fun mount(props: ProductPageProps): Pair<ProductPageState, List<Command>> =
2138:     Pair(
2139:         ProductPageState(product = props.product),
2140:         listOf(
2141:             Command.async("related") { ProductService.getRelated(props.product.id, limit = 4) },
2142:             Command.async("reviews") { ReviewService.getForProduct(props.product.id, limit = 10) }
2143:         )
2144:     )
2145: 
2146: fun handle_info(msg: AsyncResult<"related", List<Product>>, state: ProductPageState): ProductPageState =
2147:     state.copy(relatedProducts = when (msg) {
2148:         is Ok  -> AsyncValue.ready(msg.value)
2149:         is Err -> AsyncValue.error(msg.reason.toString())
2150:     })
2151: 
2152: fun handle_info(msg: AsyncResult<"reviews", List<Review>>, state: ProductPageState): ProductPageState =
2153:     state.copy(reviews = when (msg) {
2154:         is Ok  -> AsyncValue.ready(msg.value)
2155:         is Err -> AsyncValue.error(msg.reason.toString())
2156:     })
2157: ```
2158: 
2159: ```kotlin
2160: ---
2161: 
2162: <div class="product-page">
2163:     <ProductHero product={state.product} />
2164: 
2165:     <section class="product-page__related">
2166:         <h2>Related Products</h2>
2167:         { when (state.relatedProducts) {
2168:             is AsyncValue.Loading -> <ProductGridSkeleton count={4} />
2169:             is AsyncValue.Error   -> <p class="error">{ state.relatedProducts.message }</p>
2170:             is AsyncValue.Ready   -> <ProductGrid products={state.relatedProducts.value} />
2171:         } }
2172:     </section>
2173: 
2174:     <section class="product-page__reviews">
2175:         <h2>Reviews</h2>
2176:         { when (state.reviews) {
2177:             is AsyncValue.Loading -> <ReviewListSkeleton count={3} />
2178:             is AsyncValue.Error   -> <p class="error">Could not load reviews</p>
2179:             is AsyncValue.Ready   -> <ReviewList reviews={state.reviews.value} />
2180:         } }
2181:     </section>
2182: </div>
2183: ```
2184: 
2185: **`AsyncValue<T>` is a sealed class provided by the aKt standard library:**
2186: 
2187: ```kotlin
2188: sealed class AsyncValue<out T> {
2189:     object Loading : AsyncValue<Nothing>()
2190:     data class Error(val message: String) : AsyncValue<Nothing>()
2191:     data class Ready<T>(val value: T) : AsyncValue<T>()
2192: 
2193:     companion object {
2194:         fun loading(): AsyncValue<Nothing> = Loading
2195:         fun <T> ready(value: T): AsyncValue<T> = Ready(value)
2196:         fun error(message: String): AsyncValue<Nothing> = Error(message)
2197:     }
2198: }
2199: ```

2202: 
2203: ## 11.7 — File-Based Routing
2204: 
2205: ### Directory Structure
2206: 
2207: aKt follows Next.js's App Router conventions adapted for the BEAM. Routes are declared by file position in the `pages/` directory:
2208: 
2209: ```
2210: pages/
2211:   index.akt                   → GET /
2212:   about.akt                   → GET /about
2213:   users/
2214:     index.akt                 → GET /users
2215:     new.akt                   → GET /users/new
2216:     [id].akt                  → GET /users/:id
2217:     [id]/
2218:       edit.akt                → GET /users/:id/edit
2219:       posts.akt               → GET /users/:id/posts
2220:       posts/
2221:         [postId].akt          → GET /users/:id/posts/:postId
2222:   blog/
2223:     [...slug].akt             → GET /blog/* (wildcard, captures all segments)
2224:   api/                        → (API routes — handled by Ping directly, not aKt)
2225:     users.akt                 → REST endpoint, not a LiveComponent
2226: ```
2227: 
2228: Dynamic segments are declared with `[paramName]`. The parameter is available in the component as `params.id`, `params.postId`, etc. The type of all route parameters is `String`; parsing to other types is done explicitly:
2229: 
2230: ```kotlin
2231: // pages/users/[id].akt
2232: 
2233: props UserPageProps {
2234:     val id: String  // Automatically populated from route
2235: }
2236: 
2237: // OR with explicit parsing:
2238: props UserPageProps {
2239:     val id: String
2240: }
2241: 
2242: suspend fun loadData(props: UserPageProps): UserPageState {
2243:     val userId = props.id.toLongOrNull()
2244:         ?: throw NotFoundException("Invalid user id: ${props.id}")
2245:     val user = UserService.getById(userId)
2246:         ?: throw NotFoundException("User not found: $userId")
2247:     return UserPageState(user = user)
2248: }
2249: ```
2250: 
2251: Wildcard routes `[...slug]` capture all remaining path segments as a `List<String>`:
2252: 
2253: ```kotlin
2254: // pages/blog/[...slug].akt
2255: 
2256: props BlogPageProps {
2257:     val slug: List<String>  // e.g., ["2024", "06", "my-post-title"]
2258: }
2259: ```
2260: 
2261: ### Layouts
2262: 
2263: `_layout.akt` wraps all routes in its directory. Layouts are composable: a layout in a subdirectory wraps its routes and is itself wrapped by the parent directory's layout.
2264: 
2265: ```
2266: pages/
2267:   _layout.akt        → Root layout (wraps everything)
2268:   index.akt
2269:   users/
2270:     _layout.akt      → Users layout (wraps all /users/* routes)
2271:     index.akt
2272:     [id].akt
2273: ```
2274: 
2275: ```kotlin
2276: // pages/_layout.akt — Root layout
2277:

2294:             },

2296:         )
2297:     )
2298: 
2299: fun handle_info(msg: AsyncResult<"load_notifications", List<Notification>>, state: RootLayoutState): RootLayoutState =
2300:     state.copy(notifications = msg.value)
2301: 
2302: fun handle_info(msg: NewNotification, state: RootLayoutState): RootLayoutState =
2303:     state.copy(notifications = listOf(msg.notification) + state.notifications)
2304: 
2305: ---
2306: 
2307: <div class="app">
2308:     <header class="app__header">
2309:         <SiteNav session={props.session} />
2310:         <NotificationBell count={state.notifications.size} />
2311:     </header>
2312:     <main class="app__main">

2314:     </main>

2321: ```kotlin
2322: // pages/users/_layout.akt — Users section layout
2323: 
2324: props UsersLayoutProps {
2325:     val session: Session
2326: }
2327:

2339: 
2340: The root layout receives the full `children` of the page. Nested layouts receive the page content as their children and are themselves the `children` of the root layout. The composition is:
2341: 
2342: ```
2343: RootLayout
2344:   └── UsersLayout (children of RootLayout)
2345:         └── UserPage (children of UsersLayout)
2346: ```
2347: 
2348: ### Loading and Error States
2349: 
2350: `_loading.akt` is rendered while the page's `loadData` is executing. It receives the route params but not the loaded data:
2351: 
2352: ```kotlin
2353: // pages/users/[id]/_loading.akt
2354: 
2355: props UserPageLoadingProps {
2356:     val id: String
2357: }
2358: 
2359: ---
2360: 
2361: <div class="user-page-skeleton">
2362:     <div class="skeleton skeleton--avatar" aria-hidden="true" />
2363:     <div class="skeleton skeleton--title" aria-hidden="true" />
2364:     <div class="skeleton skeleton--text" aria-hidden="true" />
2365:     <div class="skeleton skeleton--text" aria-hidden="true" />
2366:     <p class="sr-only" role="status">Loading user profile...</p>
2367: </div>
2368: ```
2369: 
2370: `_error.akt` is rendered when the page's `loadData` throws an exception or when the component's GenServer crashes and restarts:
2371: 
2372: ```kotlin
2373: // pages/users/[id]/_error.akt
2374: 
2375: props UserPageErrorProps {
2376:     val error: AktError    // The caught exception
2377:     val id: String         // Route params still available
2378: }
2379: 
2380: ---
2381: 
2382: <div class="error-state" role="alert">
2383:     { when (props.error) {
2384:         is NotFoundException -> (
2385:             <div>
2386:                 <h2>User Not Found</h2>
2387:                 <p>No user exists with ID { props.id }.</p>
2388:                 <a href="/users">Back to Users</a>
2389:             </div>
2390:         )
2391:         is AuthorizationException -> (
2392:             <div>
2393:                 <h2>Access Denied</h2>
2394:                 <p>You do not have permission to view this profile.</p>
2395:             </div>
2396:         )
2397:         else -> (
2398:             <div>
2399:                 <h2>Something went wrong</h2>
2400:                 <p>An unexpected error occurred. Please try again.</p>
2401:                 <button onClick={handleRetry}>Retry</button>
2402:             </div>
2403:         )
2404:     } }
2405: </div>
2406: ```
2407: 
2408: ### Integration with Ping
2409: 
2410: The Ping router DSL is generated automatically from the `pages/` directory structure. The developer does not write router entries for aKt pages — the compiler emits them:
2411: 
2412: **Generated Ping router (illustrative; not written by hand):**
2413: 
2414: ```kotlin
2415: // Generated by aKt compiler — do not edit manually
2416: // .build/generated/router.kore
2417: 
2418: router {
2419:     pipeline("live") {
2420:         plug(AktRuntime.LiveSocket)
2421:         plug(AktRuntime.SessionMiddleware)
2422:     }
2423: 
2424:     scope("/", pipeline = "live") {
2425:         live("/",            'KorE.Pages.Index')
2426:         live("/about",       'KorE.Pages.About')
2427: 
2428:         live("/users",       'KorE.Pages.Users.Index')
2429:         live("/users/new",   'KorE.Pages.Users.New')
2430:         live("/users/:id",   'KorE.Pages.Users.Id',      params = ["id"])
2431:         live("/users/:id/edit", 'KorE.Pages.Users.Id.Edit', params = ["id"])
2432: 
2433:         live("/blog/*slug",  'KorE.Pages.Blog.Slug',     params = ["slug"])
2434:     }
2435: }
2436: ```
2437: 
2438: The `live/3` function is a Ping extension for aKt routes. It registers both the initial HTTP GET handler (which renders the static HTML shell and initiates the WebSocket connection) and the WebSocket event handler for the component.
2439: 
2440: ### Programmatic Navigation
2441: 
2442: Navigation inside aKt components uses `Command.navigate` and `Command.patch`:
2443: 
2444: ```kotlin
2445: // Full navigation: unmounts current component, mounts new one
2446: // Equivalent to LiveView's push_navigate
2447: fun handleViewUser(userId: String, state: UserListState): Pair<UserListState, List<Command>> =
2448:     Pair(state, listOf(Command.navigate("/users/$userId")))
2449: 
2450: // Patch: updates URL and props without unmounting the component
2451: // Equivalent to LiveView's push_patch
2452: // Use when you're navigating within the same component (pagination, filters, etc.)
2453: fun handlePageChange(page: Int, state: UserListState): Pair<UserListState, List<Command>> =
2454:     Pair(state.copy(loading = true), listOf(Command.patch("/users?page=$page")))
2455: 
2456: // Patch triggers 'update' on the component with new params
2457: fun update(newProps: UserListProps, oldProps: UserListProps, state: UserListState): Pair<UserListState, List<Command>> =
2458:     if (newProps.page != oldProps.page) {
2459:         Pair(
2460:             state.copy(loading = true),
2461:             listOf(Command.async("load_users") { UserService.getPage(newProps.page) })
2462:         )
2463:     } else {
2464:         Pair(state, emptyList())
2465:     }
2466: ```
2467: 
2468: Navigation targets are validated at compile time when string literals are used. `Command.navigate("/users")` will produce a compile warning if `/users` does not match any page in the `pages/` directory. Dynamic paths constructed at runtime are not validated at compile time.
2469: 
2470: ### Page-Level Data Loading
2471: 
2472: The `loadData` function is the aKt equivalent of Next.js's `getServerSideProps`. It runs on the server before the component is mounted, and its result becomes the initial state:
2473: 
2474: ```kotlin
2475: // pages/products/[id].akt
2476: 
2477: props ProductPageProps {
2478:     val id: String
2479: }
2480: 
2481: data class ProductPageState(
2482:     val product: Product,
2483:     val relatedProducts: List<Product>,
2484:     val inStock: Boolean,
2485:     val reviews: AsyncValue<List<Review>> = AsyncValue.loading()
2486: )
2487: 
2488: // Runs before mount — blocks initial HTML until resolved
2489: // Throws NotFoundException → shows _error.akt
2490: // Throws AuthorizationException → redirects to login
2491: suspend fun loadData(props: ProductPageProps, session: Session): ProductPageState {
2492:     val id = props.id.toLongOrNull() ?: throw NotFoundException()
2493:     val (product, related, stock) = awaitAll(
2494:         async { ProductService.getById(id) ?: throw NotFoundException() },
2495:         async { ProductService.getRelated(id, limit = 4) },
2496:         async { InventoryService.checkStock(id) }
2497:     )
2498:     return ProductPageState(product = product, relatedProducts = related, inStock = stock)
2499: }
2500: 
2501: fun mount(props: ProductPageProps, initialState: ProductPageState): Pair<ProductPageState, List<Command>> =
2502:     Pair(
2503:         initialState,
2504:         listOf(Command.async("load_reviews") { ReviewService.getForProduct(props.id.toLong()!!, limit = 10) })
2505:     )
2506: ```
2507: 
2508: `loadData` receives the route props (including all path params and query params) and the current session. It may be `suspend` (blocking async) or regular (synchronous). Throwing a `NotFoundException` renders `_error.akt`. Returning `Command.redirect(...)` is done via a special redirect exception: `throw RedirectException("/login")`.
2509: 
2510: Query parameters are exposed as props when declared:
2511: 
2512: ```kotlin
2513: // pages/users/index.akt
2514: 
2515: props UsersIndexProps {
2516:     val page: Int = 1      // ?page=2 → props.page = 2
2517:     val search: String = ""  // ?search=alice → props.search = "alice"
2518:     val sort: SortOrder = .nameAsc
2519: }
2520: ```
2521: 
2522: The compiler generates the query param parsing from the props declaration. String types accept the raw value; typed props use the type's `fromString` conversion. If the query param cannot be parsed to the declared type, the default value is used.
2523: 
2524: ---
2525: 
2526: ## 11.8 — Async Data Loading
2527: 
2528: ### `assign_async` Equivalent: `Command.async`
2529: 
2530: Phoenix LiveView's `assign_async` runs a function asynchronously and updates the socket assigns when it completes. aKt's equivalent is `Command.async`:
2531: 
2532: ```kotlin
2533: // LiveView (Elixir)
2534: assign_async(socket, [:user, :posts], fn ->
2535:     {:ok, %{
2536:         user: Accounts.get_user!(user_id),
2537:         posts: Posts.list_posts(user_id)
2538:     }}
2539: end)
2540: 
2541: // aKt equivalent
2542: Command.async("load_user_data") {
2543:     val user = UserService.getById(userId)
2544:     val posts = PostService.getByUser(userId)
2545:     UserData(user = user, posts = posts)
2546: }
2547: ```
2548: 
2549: `Command.async(name, block)` creates an asynchronous command. The block runs in a separate coroutine on the BEAM. When it completes, it sends an `AsyncResult<name, T>` message to the component process, which is handled by `handle_info`.
2550: 
2551: **Naming matters**: The name string is used as a type-level tag for the result. The compiler verifies that every `Command.async("name")` call has a corresponding `handle_info(msg: AsyncResult<"name", T>)` handler. An `Command.async` without a corresponding handler is a compile warning.
2552: 
2553: **Cancellation**: If the component is unmounted or a new `Command.async("name")` is issued before the previous one completes, the previous one's result is discarded (not sent to the component). This prevents stale data races.
2554: 
2555: ```kotlin
2556: // Full async loading example
2557: data class UserDashboardState(
2558:     val user: AsyncValue<User> = AsyncValue.loading(),
2559:     val stats: AsyncValue<UserStats> = AsyncValue.loading(),
2560:     val recentActivity: AsyncValue<List<Activity>> = AsyncValue.loading()
2561: )
2562: 
2563: fun mount(props: UserDashboardProps): Pair<UserDashboardState, List<Command>> =
2564:     Pair(
2565:         UserDashboardState(),
2566:         listOf(
2567:             Command.async("load_user") { UserService.getById(props.userId) },
2568:             Command.async("load_stats") { StatsService.getForUser(props.userId) },
2569:             Command.async("load_activity") { ActivityService.getRecent(props.userId, limit = 10) }
2570:         )
2571:     )
2572: 
2573: fun handle_info(msg: AsyncResult<"load_user", User>, state: UserDashboardState): UserDashboardState =
2574:     state.copy(user = when (msg) {
2575:         is Ok  -> AsyncValue.ready(msg.value)
2576:         is Err -> AsyncValue.error(msg.reason.toString())
2577:     })
2578: 
2579: fun handle_info(msg: AsyncResult<"load_stats", UserStats>, state: UserDashboardState): UserDashboardState =
2580:     state.copy(stats = when (msg) {
2581:         is Ok  -> AsyncValue.ready(msg.value)
2582:         is Err -> AsyncValue.error(msg.reason.toString())
2583:     })
2584: 
2585: fun handle_info(msg: AsyncResult<"load_activity", List<Activity>>, state: UserDashboardState): UserDashboardState =
2586:     state.copy(recentActivity = when (msg) {
2587:         is Ok  -> AsyncValue.ready(msg.value)
2588:         is Err -> AsyncValue.error(msg.reason.toString())
2589:     })
2590: ```
2591: 
2592: ### Loading States
2593: 
2594: The `AsyncValue<T>` sealed class (defined in Section 11.6) provides the three states. The template `when` expression handles them:
2595: 
2596: ```kotlin
2597: ---
2598: 
2599: <div class="user-dashboard">
2600:     { when (state.user) {
2601:         is AsyncValue.Loading -> <div class="skeleton skeleton--profile" aria-label="Loading profile..." />
2602:         is AsyncValue.Error   -> <ErrorCard message={state.user.message} onRetry={handleRetryUser} />
2603:         is AsyncValue.Ready   -> <UserProfileCard user={state.user.value} />
2604:     } }
2605: 
2606:     <div class="dashboard-stats">
2607:         { when (state.stats) {
2608:             is AsyncValue.Loading -> <StatsSkeleton />
2609:             is AsyncValue.Error   -> <p class="error">Stats unavailable</p>
2610:             is AsyncValue.Ready   -> <StatsGrid stats={state.stats.value} />
2611:         } }
2612:     </div>
2613: 
2614:     <section class="recent-activity">
2615:         <h2>Recent Activity</h2>
2616:         { when (state.recentActivity) {
2617:             is AsyncValue.Loading -> <ActivityListSkeleton />
2618:             is AsyncValue.Error   -> <p class="error">Activity unavailable</p>
2619:             is AsyncValue.Ready when state.recentActivity.value.isEmpty() -> (
2620:                 <p class="empty">No recent activity</p>
2621:             )
2622:             is AsyncValue.Ready   -> (
2623:                 <ul class="activity-list">
2624:                     {for activity in state.recentActivity.value}
2625:                         <li key={activity.id}><ActivityItem activity={activity} /></li>
2626:                     {/for}
2627:                 </ul>
2628:             )
2629:         } }
2630:     </section>
2631: </div>
2632: ```
2633: 
2634: ### Stale Data While Reloading
2635: 
2636: To show stale data while refreshing (e.g., for a pull-to-refresh or auto-refresh pattern), extend `AsyncValue` with a `Refreshing` state:
2637: 
2638: ```kotlin
2639: sealed class AsyncValue<out T> {
2640:     object Loading : AsyncValue<Nothing>()
2641:     data class Error(val message: String) : AsyncValue<Nothing>()
2642:     data class Ready<T>(val value: T) : AsyncValue<T>()
2643:     data class Refreshing<T>(val staleValue: T) : AsyncValue<T>()
2644: 
2645:     val isLoading: Boolean get() = this is Loading || this is Refreshing
2646:     val valueOrNull: T? get() = when (this) {
2647:         is Ready -> value
2648:         is Refreshing -> staleValue
2649:         else -> null
2650:     }
2651: }
2652: 
2653: fun handleRefresh(state: FeedState, props: FeedProps): Pair<FeedState, List<Command>> =
2654:     Pair(
2655:         state.copy(
2656:             posts = when (val p = state.posts) {
2657:                 is AsyncValue.Ready -> AsyncValue.Refreshing(p.value)
2658:                 else -> AsyncValue.Loading
2659:             }
2660:         ),
2661:         listOf(Command.async("load_posts") { PostService.getRecent(props.userId) })
2662:     )
2663: ```
2664: 
2665: ```kotlin
2666: ---
2667: 
2668: <div class="feed">
2669:     <div class="feed__header">
2670:         <h2>Your Feed</h2>
2671:         <button
2672:             onClick={handleRefresh}
2673:             disabled={state.posts.isLoading}
2674:             aria-label="Refresh feed"
2675:         >
2676:             { if (state.posts.isLoading) "Refreshing..." else "Refresh" }
2677:         </button>
2678:     </div>
2679: 
2680:     { when (state.posts) {
2681:         is AsyncValue.Loading    -> <FeedSkeleton />
2682:         is AsyncValue.Refreshing -> (
2683:             // Show stale data with a refreshing indicator
2684:             <>
2685:                 <div class="feed__refreshing-banner" role="status" aria-live="polite">
2686:                     Refreshing...
2687:                 </div>
2688:                 <PostList posts={state.posts.staleValue} />
2689:             </>
2690:         )
2691:         is AsyncValue.Ready      -> <PostList posts={state.posts.value} />
2692:         is AsyncValue.Error      -> <FeedError message={state.posts.message} onRetry={handleRefresh} />
2693:     } }
2694: </div>
2695: ```
2696: 
2697: ### Parallel Data Loading
2698: 
2699: `Command.async` calls in a list execute in parallel automatically — each one spawns a separate coroutine. They resolve independently and trigger separate `handle_info` calls:
