1016:     mounted() {
1017:         // Register a handler for the "highlight" event from the server
1018:         this.handleEvent("highlight", ({ index }) => {
1019:             this.chart.setHighlight(index)
1020:         })
1021:     }
1022: }
1023: ```
1024: 
1025: The aKt runtime receives the server-push message, looks up all hook instances for the component, filters to those named `Chart`, and calls `handleEvent("highlight", payload)` on each.
1026: 
1027: ### Client Sending an Event to the Server
1028: 
1029: ```javascript
1030: const Chart = {
1031:     mounted() {
1032:         this.el.addEventListener("click", (e) => {
1033:             const index = getIndexFromPoint(e.offsetX, e.offsetY, this.chart)
1034:             // Push an event to the server component that owns this hook
1035:             this.pushEvent("chart_clicked", { index })
1036:         })
1037:     }
1038: }
1039: ```
1040: 
1041: ### Server Receiving the Event
1042: 
1043: ```kotlin
1044: // handle_info receives HookEvent messages
1045: fun handle_info(msg: HookEvent<"chart_clicked">, state: DashState): DashState =
1046:     state.copy(selectedIndex = msg.payload["index"] as Int)
1047: ```
1048: 
1049: `HookEvent<"chart_clicked">` is a KorE type that the compiler recognizes and routes to this `handle_info` function when the BEAM process receives a `{hook_event, "chart_clicked", Payload}` message. The `msg.payload` field is a `Map<String, Any>` deserialized from the JSON payload.
1050: 
1051: ### The Wire Format
1052: 
1053: ```
1054: Client → Server:
1055: {"type":"hook_event","hook":"Chart","name":"chart_clicked","payload":{"index":3}}
1056: 
1057: Server → Client:
1058: {"type":"hook_event","hook":"Chart","name":"highlight","payload":{"index":3}}
1059: ```
1060: 
1061: ---
1062: 
1063: ## `use client` Components — Full Reference
1064: 
1065: ### What `use client` Means
1066: 
1067: When the compiler sees `use client` as the first line of a `.akt` file, it routes the entire file to the TypeScript/JavaScript backend instead of the Erlang backend. The component is compiled to a JS bundle rather than BEAM bytecode.
1068: 
1069: However, the server still participates in two ways:
1070: 1. The initial HTML is server-rendered by executing the component's `mount` state computation on the server and building the initial DOM string.
1071: 2. Callbacks (event handlers passed as props from a parent server component) are serialized as event bindings and dispatched back to the parent server component over WebSocket when invoked.
1072: 
1073: ### What the aKt-to-TS Compiler Generates
1074: 
1075: For a `use client` component, the compiler emits a TypeScript class:
1076: 
1077: ```typescript
1078: // Generated TypeScript for a use client SortableList component
1079: export class SortableList {
1080:     private state: SortableListState
1081:     private props: SortableListProps
1082:     private el: HTMLElement
1083: 
1084:     constructor(el: HTMLElement, props: SortableListProps) {
1085:         this.el = el
1086:         this.props = props
1087:         this.state = this.mount(props)
1088:         this.render()
1089:     }
1090: 
1091:     private mount(props: SortableListProps): SortableListState {
1092:         return { items: props.items, dragging: null }
1093:     }
1094: 
1095:     private setState(newState: SortableListState) {
1096:         this.state = newState
1097:         this.render()
1098:     }
1099: 
1100:     // Generated from KorE template
1101:     private render() {
1102:         this.el.innerHTML = this.renderTemplate(this.state, this.props)
1103:         this.attachEvents()
1104:     }
1105: 
1106:     private renderTemplate(state: SortableListState, props: SortableListProps): string {
1107:         // ... generated from template AST
1108:     }
1109: 
1110:     private attachEvents() {
1111:         // ... generated event bindings
1112:     }
1113: 
1114:     // Public: called by runtime when props change from server
1115:     update(newProps: Partial<SortableListProps>) {
1116:         this.props = { ...this.props, ...newProps }
1117:         this.render()
1118:     }
1119: }
1120: ```
1121: 
1122: The compiled JS bundle is hashed and placed in the `priv/static/akt/` directory. The server knows the bundle path and emits it in the island mount metadata.
1123: 
1124: ### Props Serialization
1125: 
1126: When a parent server component renders a `use client` island, it embeds the props as JSON in a `data-akt-props` attribute and the component name in a `data-akt-island` attribute:
1127: 
1128: ```html
1129: <div
1130:   data-akt-island="SortableList"
1131:   data-akt-bundle="/akt/sortable_list-a3f9e2.js"
1132:   data-akt-props='{"items":["Alice","Bob","Charlie"],"onReorder":"__cb:reorder_users"}'
1133: >
1134:   <!-- Initial server-rendered HTML -->
1135:   <ul>
1136:     <li data-id="alice">Alice</li>
1137:     <li data-id="bob">Bob</li>
1138:     <li data-id="charlie">Charlie</li>
1139:   </ul>
1140: </div>
1141: ```
1142: 
1143: The client runtime finds all `[data-akt-island]` elements on page load, imports the bundle at `data-akt-bundle`, deserializes `data-akt-props`, and calls `hydrate(element, props)`. Hydration reuses the server-rendered HTML rather than replacing it (progressive hydration), attaching event listeners and initializing state without touching the DOM.
1144: 
1145: ### Callback Serialization
1146: 
1147: When a parent server component passes a callback prop to a `use client` component:
1148: 
1149: ```kotlin
1150: // In parent server component template
1151: <SortableList
1152:     items={state.users.map { it.name }}
1153:     onReorder={ ids -> handleReorder(ids, state) }
1154: />
1155: ```
1156: 
1157: The compiler detects that `onReorder` is a function prop passed to a `use client` component. It cannot serialize the lambda as a function. Instead, it:
1158: 
1159: 1. Generates a unique callback binding name: `"__cb:reorder_users"` (derived from the prop name and component context)
1160: 2. Serializes the prop as the string `"__cb:reorder_users"` in the JSON props
1161: 3. Registers a `handle_info` handler in the parent GenServer for the `callback_invoked` message with this binding name
1162: 
1163: On the client side, the runtime deserializes props and recognizes `"__cb:reorder_users"` as a callback binding (the `__cb:` prefix is the discriminant). It replaces the string with a function that calls `this.pushEventTo(parentSelector, "callback_invoked", { name: "reorder_users", args: [...] })`.
1164: 
1165: When invoked in the client component:
1166: 
1167: ```typescript
1168: // Inside SortableList
1169: this.props.onReorder(newOrderIds)
1170: // → calls: pushEventTo("#parent-123", "callback_invoked", { name: "reorder_users", args: [newOrderIds] })
1171: ```
1172: 
1173: The server parent receives:
1174: 
1175: ```kotlin
1176: fun handle_info(msg: CallbackInvoked<"reorder_users">, state: ParentState): ParentState =
1177:     handleReorder(msg.args[0] as List<String>, state)
1178: ```
1179: 
1180: ### Complete `use client` Example
1181: 
1182: ```kotlin
1183: // components/SortableList.akt
1184: use client
1185: 
1186: @Component
1187: class SortableList {
1188: 
1189:     props {
1190:         val items: List<String>
1191:         val onReorder: (List<String>) -> Unit
1192:     }
1193: 
1194:     data class SortableState(
1195:         val items: List<String>,
1196:         val draggingIndex: Int? = null
1197:     )
1198: 
1199:     fun mount(props: SortableListProps): SortableState =
1200:         SortableState(items = props.items)
1201: 
1202:     fun dragStart(event: DragEvent, state: SortableState): SortableState =
1203:         state.copy(draggingIndex = event.target.dataset["index"]?.toInt())
1204: 
1205:     fun dragEnd(event: DragEvent, state: SortableState): SortableState {
1206:         val newOrder = reorder(state.items, state.draggingIndex ?: return state, event.dropIndex)
1207:         props.onReorder(newOrder)
1208:         return state.copy(items = newOrder, draggingIndex = null)
1209:     }
1210: }
1211: 
1212: ---
1213: 
1214: <ul class="sortable-list">
1215:   @for ((index, item) in state.items) {
1216:     <li
1217:       key={index.toString()}
1218:       class={ if (state.draggingIndex == index) "dragging" else "" }
1219:       data-index={index.toString()}
1220:       onDragStart={dragStart}
1221:       onDragEnd={dragEnd}
1222:       draggable
1223:     >
1224:       { item }
1225:     </li>
1226:   }
1227: </ul>
1228: ```
1229: 
1230: ---
1231: 
1232: ## File Uploads
1233: 
1234: ### Declaring an Upload
1235: 
1236: File uploads are declared in an event handler using `Command.allow_upload`. The declaration specifies the input name, accepted MIME types, maximum file size, and maximum number of files.
1237: 
1238: ```kotlin
1239: // In PageComponent.akt logic section
1240: 
1241: data class UploadState(
1242:     val uploads: AsyncValue<List<String>> = AsyncValue.Loading,
1243:     val uploadProgress: Map<String, Int> = emptyMap()
1244: )
1245: 
1246: fun handleAllowUpload(event: ClickEvent, state: UploadState): Pair<UploadState, List<Command>> =
1247:     Pair(state, listOf(
1248:         Command.allow_upload("avatar",
1249:             accept = listOf("image/png", "image/jpeg"),
1250:             maxSize = 5 * 1024 * 1024,   // 5 MB
1251:             maxFiles = 1
1252:         )
1253:     ))
1254: 
1255: fun handle_info(msg: UploadProgress<"avatar">, state: UploadState): UploadState =
1256:     state.copy(uploadProgress = state.uploadProgress + (msg.ref to msg.percent))
1257: 
1258: fun handle_info(msg: UploadComplete<"avatar">, state: UploadState): Pair<UploadState, List<Command>> =
1259:     Pair(
1260:         state.copy(uploads = AsyncValue.Loading),
1261:         listOf(Command.consume_uploaded("avatar") { entries ->
1262:             entries.map { entry ->
1263:                 val dest = "/uploads/${entry.filename}"
1264:                 entry.copyTo(dest)
1265:                 dest
1266:             }
1267:         })
1268:     )
1269: 
1270: fun handle_info(msg: AsyncResult<"consume_avatar", List<String>>, state: UploadState): UploadState =
1271:     state.copy(uploads = AsyncValue.Ready(msg.value))
1272: ```
1273: 
1274: ### The Template
1275: 
1276: ```kotlin
1277: <div class="upload-area">
1278:   <input
1279:     type="file"
1280:     phx-upload="avatar"
1281:     accept="image/png, image/jpeg"
1282:   />
1283: 
1284:   @if (state.uploadProgress.isNotEmpty()) {
1285:     @for ((ref, percent) in state.uploadProgress) {
1286:       <div class="progress-bar">
1287:         <div class="progress-fill" style="width: {percent}%"></div>
1288:       </div>
1289:     }
1290:   }
1291: 
1292:   @when (state.uploads) {
1293:     is AsyncValue.Ready -> {
1294:       <p>Uploaded: { state.uploads.value.joinToString(", ") }</p>
1295:     }
1296:     is AsyncValue.Error -> {
1297:       <p class="error">Upload failed: { state.uploads.message }</p>
1298:     }
1299:     else -> {}
1300:   }
1301: </div>
1302: ```
1303: 
1304: ### How It Works
1305: 
1306: `Command.allow_upload` registers an upload slot in the component's GenServer. The aKt runtime on the client detects the `phx-upload` attribute, and when the user selects files, begins a chunked upload over the WebSocket (not a separate HTTP request). Progress messages arrive as `UploadProgress<"avatar">` `handle_info` calls. When all chunks are received, `UploadComplete<"avatar">` fires. `Command.consume_uploaded` runs the provided lambda in an async task that receives the completed upload entries — temporary file handles — and can move them to permanent storage.
1307: 
1308: ---
1309: 
1310: ## Script Tags and Global JS
1311: 
1312: ### `<script>` in `.akt` Files
1313: 
1314: `<script>` tags are permitted only in layout files (`_layout.akt`) and page files (files in `pages/`). They are not permitted inside component files (files in `components/`). The tag must appear as a direct child of the template root, not nested inside elements.
1315: 
1316: ```kotlin
1317: // pages/_layout.akt — allowed
1318: ---
1319: <html>
1320:   <head>
1321:     <script src="/akt/runtime.js" defer></script>
1322:     <script>
1323:       window.analyticsId = "UA-XXXXX"
1324:     </script>
1325:   </head>
1326:   <body>
1327:     <slot />
1328:   </body>
1329: </html>
1330: ```
1331: 
1332: Inline `<script>` tags in pages run once when the page is first loaded. They do not re-run on LiveView patches. If you need to run JS on each patch, use a hook.
1333: 
1334: ### Global JS Includes
1335: 
1336: Global scripts and stylesheets belong in `pages/_layout.akt`'s `<head>` section. The `akt-runtime` bundle must be included here:
1337: 
1338: ```kotlin
1339: <head>
1340:   <meta charset="utf-8" />
1341:   <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
1342:   <link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/app.css" />
1343:   <script src="/assets/akt-runtime.js" defer></script>
1344:   <script src="/assets/app.js" defer></script>
1345: </head>
1346: ```
1347: 
1348: ### Page-Specific Head Elements
1349: 
1350: To inject page-specific `<title>`, `<meta>`, or `<link>` tags from a page component, use the `<head>` slot that the root layout exposes:
1351: 
1352: ```kotlin
1353: // pages/_layout.akt template section
1354: <html>
1355:   <head>
1356:     <slot name="head" />           ← layout declares the head slot
1357:     <link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/app.css" />
1358:     <script src="/assets/akt-runtime.js" defer></script>
1359:   </head>
1360:   <body><slot /></body>
1361: </html>
1362: ```
1363: 
1364: ```kotlin
1365: // pages/users/[id].akt template section
1366: <_layout>
1367:   <template slot="head">          ← page fills the head slot
1368:     <title>{ state.user.name } — MyApp</title>
1369:     <meta name="description" content={state.user.bio} />
1370:   </template>
1371: 
1372:   <div class="profile">
1373:     ...
1374:   </div>
1375: </_layout>
1376: ```
1377: 
1378: The compiler verifies at compile time that the slot names match between the layout's `<slot name="...">` declarations and the page's `<template slot="...">` usages.
1379: 
1380: ---
1381: 
1382: # 11.12 — Language Feature Requirements Inventory
1383: 
1384: This section is a precise, exhaustive list of everything aKt demands from the KorE compiler. Each entry specifies what is required, what the compiler must produce, which compiler phase handles it, and any open design questions.
1385: 
1386: ---
1387: 
1388: ## 1. `.akt` File Format Recognition
1389: 
1390: **What it is**: The KorE compiler must distinguish `.akt` files from `.kore` files and route them through the aKt compiler pipeline.
1391: 
1392: **What it must do**: The compiler's file loader checks the file extension. `.kore` files go through the standard KorE pipeline. `.akt` files are handed to the aKt pre-processor, which performs the `---` split before any further parsing. If a `.akt` file contains no `---` line, the compiler emits `E0001` and halts processing of that file. The split is on the first occurrence of a line equal to `"---"` after trimming trailing `\r` (for Windows line endings). Everything strictly above that line is the logic text; everything strictly below is the template text.
1393: 
1394: **Compiler phase**: File loading / pre-processing, before the parse phase.
1395: 
1396: **Open questions**: Should `.akt` files be permitted to import from `.kore` files and vice versa? Currently yes — the module system is shared. Should a `.akt` file be permitted to have no logic section (empty above `---`)? Currently yes, it produces a component with no declared handlers. Should the template section be permitted to be empty? Currently no — a component must render something.
1397: 
1398: ---
1399: 
1400: ## 2. Template AST Definition
1401: 
1402: **What it is**: The complete set of node types that the template parser produces. These are distinct from the KorE expression AST, though `ExpressionNode` embeds KorE expression nodes within it.
1403: 
1404: **What it must do**: The compiler defines the `TemplateNode` sealed class hierarchy (as shown in §11.10) in its internal type system. Template AST nodes carry `Span` references into the original `.akt` source file for diagnostics. The template AST is a separate type hierarchy from the KorE declaration/expression ASTs, but template `ExpressionNode` values contain `kore.ast.ExpressionNode` values as embedded fields.
1405: 
1406: **Compiler phase**: Defined in the compiler's IR module; populated by the template parser.
1407: 
1408: **Open questions**: Should `CommentNode` be preserved in the generated output or stripped? Current decision: stripped from the wire `Rendered` output but preserved in the AST for tooling (language server, syntax highlighting). Should there be a `RawHtmlNode` for `{@html expr}` style raw HTML injection? Currently not planned; a future security-sensitive addition.
1409: 
1410: ---
1411: 
1412: ## 3. Template Parser
1413: 
1414: **What it is**: A recursive descent parser for the template section of `.akt` files.
1415: 
1416: **What it must do**: The template parser implements the following grammar (informal notation):
1417: 
1418: ```
1419: template    ::= node*
1420: node        ::= element | component | expression | conditional | loop | fragment | text | comment
1421: element     ::= '<' LOWER_NAME attr* ('/' '>' | '>' node* '</' LOWER_NAME '>')
1422: component   ::= '<' UPPER_NAME attr* ('/' '>' | '>' slot_content '</' UPPER_NAME '>')
1423: expression  ::= '{' kore_expr '}'
1424: conditional ::= '@if' '(' kore_expr ')' '{' node* '}' ('@else' 'if' '(' kore_expr ')' '{' node* '}')* ('@else' '{' node* '}')?
1425: loop        ::= '@for' '(' binding 'in' kore_expr ')' '{' node* '}'
1426: fragment    ::= '<>' node* '</>'
1427: text        ::= [^<{@]+
1428: comment     ::= '<!--' [^-->]* '-->'
1429: attr        ::= LOWER_NAME '=' '"' text '"'         (static)
1430:              |  LOWER_NAME '=' '{' kore_expr '}'    (dynamic)
1431:              |  'on' UPPER_NAME '=' '{' kore_expr '}' (event)
1432:              |  'use:' UPPER_NAME                   (hook)
1433:              |  'key' '=' '{' kore_expr '}'         (key)
1434:              |  LOWER_NAME                          (boolean)
1435: ```
1436: 
1437: The `kore_expr` production delegates to the KorE expression parser. The template parser passes the source position and remaining input to the KorE expression parser and receives back an `ExpressionNode` and the updated position. The two parsers share the source file reference.
1438: 
1439: **Compiler phase**: Parse phase, immediately after the `---` split.
1440: 
1441: **Open questions**: Should `@for` support destructuring bindings (`@for ((a, b) in pairs)`)? Currently yes, with `(a, b)` parsed as a destructure pattern. Should `@when` (exhaustive match, akin to Kotlin `when`) be a template directive? Currently planned as `@when (expr) { is Type -> { ... } }` but not yet specified in detail.
1442: 
1443: ---
1444: 
1445: ## 4. Template Scope Resolution
1446: 
1447: **What it is**: The mechanism by which identifiers in `{ expr }` template nodes are resolved to types and values.
1448: 
1449: **What it must do**: The compiler constructs a template scope record containing:
1450: - `props`: bound to the component's props record type, always present
1451: - `state`: bound to the component's state data class type, present only for `@LiveComponent`; a reference to `state` in a `@Component` template is a hard error
1452: - All top-level function names declared in the logic section, with their function types
1453: - All names imported into the logic section's module scope
1454: 
1455: This scope is passed to the KorE type checker when checking expressions inside `ExpressionNode` values. Loop bindings (`@for (item in list)`) extend this scope within their body.
1456: 
1457: Local variable declarations (`val x = ...`) are not permitted in the template. If the KorE expression parser encounters a `val` declaration inside `{ }`, the type checker emits an error. The rationale: template expressions are purely read-only projections of state and props. Logic that requires local variables belongs in the logic section as a helper function.
1458: 
1459: **Compiler phase**: Type checking phase.
1460: 
1461: **Open questions**: Should computed properties (functions of zero arguments) declared in the logic section be accessible as `props.derivedValue` via a getter syntax, or only as function calls `derivedValue()`? Current position: only as function calls. Should the template scope support `this` as a reference to the component instance? No — there is no `this` in aKt templates.
1462: 
1463: ---
1464: 
1465: ## 5. Component Prop Type Checking
1466: 
1467: **What it is**: Verification that every `<MyComponent prop={expr}>` usage matches the component's declared `props` block.
1468: 
1469: **What it must do**: When the type checker encounters a `ComponentNode`, it:
1470: 1. Resolves `ComponentNode.name` through the import graph to find the target `.akt` file
1471: 2. Reads the target component's `props` block to build a `PropSchema`: a map of prop name → `(type, required, default)`
1472: 3. For each attribute on the `ComponentNode`:
1473:    - If `DynamicAttribute`, type-checks the expression and verifies assignability to the declared prop type
1474:    - If `StaticAttribute` (a literal string), verifies the declared prop type is `String` or a type with a `String` constructor
1475:    - Reports unknown attributes (attributes not in `PropSchema`) as errors
1476: 4. Verifies all required props (no default value, not nullable) are present; reports missing required props as errors
1477: 5. Verifies no required prop is listed twice; reports duplicate attributes as errors
1478: 
1479: Component resolution follows the module import rules. If the component is not importable (file not found, circular import, etc.), a resolution error is emitted rather than a prop error.
1480: 
1481: **Compiler phase**: Type checking phase, after import resolution.
1482: 
1483: **Open questions**: Should `data-*` attributes on component nodes be permitted (passed through to the root element)? Currently not permitted — `data-*` attributes belong on `ElementNode` values, and components control their own root element. Should `class` and `style` be mergeable across the usage site and the component's own template? Not yet designed.
1484: 
1485: ---
1486: 
1487: ## 6. Event Handler Type Verification
1488: 
1489: **What it is**: Verification that `onClick={handler}` and similar event bindings supply a function of the correct type.
1490: 
1491: **What it must do**: The compiler maintains the event-name-to-signature table shown in §11.10. For each `EventAttribute`, it:
1492: 1. Resolves the handler expression's type via the template scope
1493: 2. Looks up the expected signature for the event name
1494: 3. Verifies the handler type is assignable to either the `State`-returning or `Pair<State, List<Command>>`-returning variant
1495: 4. Emits `E0060` with found/expected types on mismatch
1496: 
1497: For `@Component` (stateless), any event attribute is immediately an error — there is no `State` type to supply.
1498: 
1499: Handler expressions may be:
1500: - A bare function reference: `onClick={increment}` — type is looked up in scope
1501: - A lambda: `onClick={ e, s -> s.copy(count = s.count + 1) }` — type is inferred
1502: - A partial application: `onClick={ handleClick(context, _, _) }` — type is checked after partial application
1503: 
1504: **Compiler phase**: Type checking phase.
1505: 
1506: **Open questions**: Should custom event names (beyond the standard DOM events) be permitted? Yes — `onCustomEvent={handler}` should be supported for component-internal events, but the type checking rules for custom events are not yet designed. Should the handler be permitted to be a `val` of function type declared in the logic section, rather than a `fun`? Yes — any expression of the correct function type is permitted.
1507: 
1508: ---
1509: 
1510: ## 7. Static/Dynamic Split Implementation
1511: 
1512: **What it is**: The algorithm that classifies every template node as static (no runtime data dependency) or dynamic (depends on `props` or `state`).
1513: 
1514: **What it must do**: The compiler performs a bottom-up walk of the template AST. For each node, it computes a `Dependency` value:
1515: 
1516: ```kotlin
1517: enum class Dependency { Static, Props, State, Both }
1518: ```
1519: 
1520: The rules:
1521: - `TextNode`: always `Static`
1522: - `CommentNode`: always `Static`
1523: - `ExpressionNode`: `Static` if the embedded KorE expression contains no references to `props` or `state`; `Props` if it references only `props.*`; `State` if it references only `state.*`; `Both` if it references both. The reference check is a free-variable analysis on the KorE expression AST.
1524: - `ElementNode`: the maximum dependency of its attributes and children
1525: - `ComponentNode`: the maximum dependency of its prop attributes
1526: - `ConditionalNode`: always at least `Props` or `State` (since conditions reference runtime data); `Static` `ConditionalNode` values are a compile-time hint that the condition should be moved to the logic section, but not an error
1527: - `LoopNode`: always at least the dependency of the collection expression
1528: - `SlotNode`: `Static` if fallback contains no dynamic nodes, otherwise the dependency of its fallback
1529: - `FragmentNode`: the maximum dependency of its children
1530: 
1531: A "static subtree" is any node with `Dependency.Static`. Static subtrees are serialized to HTML strings at compile time and stored as binary constants.
1532: 
1533: The split result is represented in the compiler IR as a `ClassifiedNode`, which wraps a `TemplateNode` with its `Dependency` and a slot index if dynamic.
1534: 
1535: **Compiler phase**: Static analysis phase, after type checking.
1536: 
1537: **Open questions**: Should function calls in template expressions be analyzed for `props`/`state` transitive dependencies (i.e., if `formatName(props.name)` calls a function, is the call classified as dynamic)? Current decision: any expression containing `props.*` or `state.*` as subexpressions is dynamic, regardless of whether it is wrapped in a function call. Tracking transitive purity through function bodies is possible but deferred.
1538: 
1539: ---
1540: 
1541: ## 8. `Rendered` Data Structure Generation
1542: 
1543: **What it is**: The exact Erlang term produced by the component's `render_template` function, and the code generation algorithm that produces it.
1544: 
1545: **What it must do**: The compiler, after the static/dynamic split, numbers each dynamic slot in template order (depth-first, left-to-right). It then generates:
1546: 
1547: 1. A list of static string segments: the HTML surrounding and between dynamic slots, stored as module-level `-define` macros
1548: 2. A `render_template(State, Props)` function body that:
1549:    - Builds the static `:s` list from the module-level constants
1550:    - Evaluates each dynamic slot expression and inserts it at the corresponding integer key
1551:    - For nested `ComponentNode` values, calls the sub-component's `render/1` function and nests the result as a nested `Rendered` map at the slot key
1552: 
1553: The static strings are computed at compile time by serializing static subtrees to HTML. Events compile to `phx-click="handler_name"` (or the equivalent for other event types). The `phx-*` attribute format is the Phoenix LiveView wire protocol, which the aKt JS runtime understands.
1554: 
1555: Nested component renders are represented as nested `Rendered` maps:
1556: 
1557: ```erlang
1558: %{
1559:   s => ["<div>", "</div>"],
1560:   0 => #{                    %% nested component's Rendered
1561:     s => ["<span>", "</span>"],
1562:     0 => <<"Alice">>
1563:   }
1564: }
1565: ```
1566: 
1567: **Compiler phase**: Code generation phase.
1568: 
1569: **Open questions**: For `ConditionalNode` and `LoopNode`, the number of dynamic slots varies at runtime. How is this represented in the `Rendered` structure? Answer: conditional branches are represented as nested `Rendered` maps at a single slot, with a special `:d` key indicating the branch index, allowing the diff algorithm to detect branch changes and send a full subtree replacement rather than a partial diff. Loops are represented as a list of `Rendered` maps. This is the same approach Phoenix LiveView uses. The full diff semantics for conditionals and loops are deferred to a later specification.
1570: 
1571: ---
1572: 
1573: ## 9. GenServer Generation for `@LiveComponent`
1574: 
1575: **What it is**: The full Erlang GenServer module the compiler emits for every `@LiveComponent`.
1576: 
1577: **What it must do**: The compiler generates a module that:
1578: 
1579: 1. Defines a `-record(component_state, {state, props, prev_rendered, socket})` for the GenServer's internal state
1580: 2. Implements `init({Props, Socket})` by calling the KorE `mount/1` function, constructing the initial `component_state`, and performing an initial render
1581: 3. Generates one `handle_call({event, Name, Payload}, ...)` clause per event handler declared in the logic section, each calling `process_commands/2` after calling the handler function
1582: 4. Generates `handle_cast({update_props, NewProps}, CS)` for prop updates
1583: 5. Generates `handle_info({async_result, Name, Result}, CS)` dispatch by pattern matching on `Name` and routing to the correct KorE `handle_info` function
1584: 6. Generates `handle_info({pubsub, Topic, Msg}, CS)` dispatch similarly
1585: 7. Generates `handle_info({hook_event, Name, Payload}, CS)` for hook events
1586: 8. Generates `terminate/2` that calls any KorE `onDestroy` function if declared
1587: 9. Generates `do_render/1` as the internal render + diff + send cycle
1588: 10. Processes `Command` values via the `process_command/2` dispatch function
1589: 
1590: **Compiler phase**: Code generation phase.
1591: 
1592: **Open questions**: Should the GenServer be supervised? Yes — each `@LiveComponent` instance is started under a `DynamicSupervisor` managed by the aKt runtime. The supervisor is generated as part of the application's supervision tree by the router code generator. Should `@LiveComponent` support `code_change/3` for hot code upgrades? Deferred — the state data class would need a migration function.
1593: 
1594: ---
1595: 
1596: ## 10. Event Binding Compilation
1597: 
1598: **What it is**: How `onClick={handler}` in a template compiles to a wire-protocol attribute in the HTML output.
1599: 
1600: **What it must do**: Each event attribute compiles to a `phx-*` prefixed attribute on the HTML element. The handler function name is serialized as the attribute value. The mapping:
1601: 
1602: | aKt attribute | Compiled HTML attribute |
1603: |---|---|
1604: | `onClick={f}` | `phx-click="f"` |
1605: | `onInput={f}` | `phx-change="f"` (mapped to change for input value tracking) |
1606: | `onChange={f}` | `phx-change="f"` |
1607: | `onSubmit={f}` | `phx-submit="f"` |
1608: | `onKeyDown={f}` | `phx-keydown="f"` |
1609: | `onKeyUp={f}` | `phx-keyup="f"` |
1610: | `onFocus={f}` | `phx-focus="f"` |
1611: | `onBlur={f}` | `phx-blur="f"` |
1612: 
1613: The event handler function name (as a string) is used as the attribute value. When the aKt JS runtime captures a `click` event on an element with `phx-click="increment"`, it sends `{type: "event", name: "increment", payload: {...}}` over the WebSocket. The GenServer's `handle_call` dispatch matches on `name` to invoke the correct handler.
1614: 
1615: Because event attributes compile to static HTML strings, they appear in the static segment of the `Rendered` structure and are never included in diffs. This means swapping event handlers at runtime by pointing `onClick` to a different function is not supported — the handler name is fixed at compile time. If conditional handler dispatch is needed, write a single handler that branches on state.
1616: 
1617: **Compiler phase**: Code generation phase (static string serialization).
1618: 
1619: **Open questions**: Should the payload include the full DOM event object, or only selected fields? Current answer: the aKt JS runtime serializes a typed subset based on the event type (e.g., `ClickEvent` gets `{x, y, button, altKey, ctrlKey, shiftKey, metaKey}`; `InputEvent` gets `{value}`). The full event object is never sent. Should debounce and throttle be declarable on event bindings? Yes — `onClick(debounce=300)={handler}` is planned but not yet specified.
1620: 
1621: ---
1622: 
1623: ## 11. `Command.async` Result Routing
1624: 
1625: **What it is**: The compile-time tracking and runtime routing of async task results to their `handle_info` handlers.
1626: 
1627: **What it must do**:
1628: 
1629: At compile time, the compiler collects all `Command.async("name")` calls in event handlers and all `handle_info(msg: AsyncResult<"name", T>)` function declarations. It builds two sets:
1630: - `asyncNames`: the set of all async task names used in `Command.async`
1631: - `handledNames`: the set of all async names with a corresponding `handle_info`
1632: 
1633: For each name in `asyncNames` not in `handledNames`, emit warning `W0030`.
1634: 
1635: At code generation time, the `handle_info` dispatch for `{async_result, Name, Result}` messages is a generated pattern match:
1636: 
1637: ```erlang
1638: handle_info({async_result, <<"loadUser">>, {ok, Result}}, CS) ->
1639:     %% dispatch to KorE handle_info for AsyncResult<"loadUser", User>
1640:     NewState = handle_info_load_user({async_result_ok, <<"loadUser">>, Result}, CS#component_state.state),
1641:     NewCS = CS#component_state{state = NewState},
1642:     {noreply, do_render(NewCS)};
1643: 
1644: handle_info({async_result, <<"loadUser">>, {error, Reason}}, CS) ->
1645:     NewState = handle_info_load_user({async_result_err, <<"loadUser">>, Reason}, CS#component_state.state),
1646:     NewCS = CS#component_state{state = NewState},
1647:     {noreply, do_render(NewCS)};
1648: ```
1649: 
1650: The `AsyncResult<"name", T>` type in KorE is a compile-time marker that generates the correct pattern match arms. The `T` type parameter is used for type checking the handler signature but erased at the Erlang level — Erlang does not enforce the type of the `Result` field.
1651: 
1652: **Compiler phase**: Static analysis (warning detection), code generation (dispatch generation).
1653: 
1654: **Open questions**: Should unhandled async results cause the GenServer to log an error at runtime rather than silently discard? Current position: yes, a `Logger.warn` call is emitted in the catch-all `handle_info` clause for unrecognized async result names, as a defense in depth measure. Should `Command.async` support a timeout? Planned: `Command.async("name", timeout = 5000) { ... }` with automatic `{async_result, Name, {error, timeout}}` on expiry.
1655: 
1656: ---
1657: 
1658: ## 12. File-Based Routing Code Generation
1659: 
1660: **What it is**: The algorithm that scans the `pages/` directory and generates a Ping router module.
1661: 
1662: **What it must do**:
1663: 
1664: 1. Recursively scan the `pages/` directory for `.akt` files
1665: 2. For each file, compute the URL path:
1666:    - `pages/index.akt` → `/`
1667:    - `pages/about.akt` → `/about`
1668:    - `pages/users/index.akt` → `/users`
1669:    - `pages/users/[id].akt` → `/users/:id`
1670:    - `pages/users/[id]/posts/[postId].akt` → `/users/:id/posts/:postId`
1671:    - `pages/[...all].akt` → `/*all` (catch-all)
1672: 3. Detect special files:
1673:    - `_layout.akt` in any directory: the layout component wrapping all pages at that level and below
1674:    - `_loading.akt`: the loading state component shown during `loadData` execution
1675:    - `_error.akt`: the error boundary component shown when `loadData` throws or a page crashes
1676: 4. Verify all page-level `.akt` files are `@LiveComponent` (not `@Component`); emit an error otherwise
1677: 5. Generate a Ping router module:
1678: 
1679: ```kotlin
1680: // Generated: MyApp.Router (Ping DSL)
1681: router {
1682:     scope("/") {
1683:         layout(MyApp.Pages.Layout)
1684: 
1685:         get("/", MyApp.Pages.Index, loading = MyApp.Pages.Loading)
1686:         get("/about", MyApp.Pages.About)
1687:         get("/users", MyApp.Pages.Users.Index)
1688:         get("/users/:id", MyApp.Pages.Users.Show, loading = MyApp.Pages.Users.Loading)
1689:         get("/users/:id/posts/:postId", MyApp.Pages.Users.Posts.Show)
1690:     }
1691: }
1692: ```
1693: 
1694: **Compiler phase**: A post-processing step that runs after all `.akt` files in `pages/` have been individually compiled, generating the router module as a final artifact.
1695: 
1696: **Open questions**: Should file-based routing support POST/PUT/DELETE routes for API endpoints? Current answer: no — aKt pages are GET-only LiveView routes. API routes are declared manually in the Ping router. Should parallel routes (Next.js-style) be supported? Not planned for initial release.

1764: - No React-style hooks (`useState`, `useEffect`, etc.). Client state lives either on the server (in `@LiveComponent`) or in `use client` island components. The runtime does not manage state.

# Session 11: aKt — The BEAM-Native Component UI Framework

---

## 11.1 — Philosophy & Design Principles

aKt exists because of a gap. LiveView solved the right problem — stateful server-rendered UI without a JavaScript framework — but it solved it for Elixir developers. React developers look at `.heex` templates and see something unfamiliar: a template-first file where the logic lives elsewhere, where the HTML is the primary artifact and the backing module is an afterthought. That's not how React developers think. They think in components: a single file, logic and markup together, props flowing down, events bubbling up.

aKt's thesis is that you can have both. You can give React developers the single-file component model they already know, the JSX-style colocation of logic and markup, the file-based routing of Next.js, the `useState`-shaped mental model — and underneath, run it all as BEAM processes communicating over WebSocket. No Node. No hydration bundle. No Virtual DOM reconciliation on the client. One GenServer per component instance, living on the server, sending minimal HTML diffs to the browser.

---

### Principle 1: React DX, BEAM Execution

The surface area of aKt is designed to be recognizable to anyone who has written a React application in the last five years. `useState` becomes an assignment on a server process. `useEffect` becomes `mount` and `handle_info`. `useContext` becomes PubSub. The mapping is not perfect — the execution model is fundamentally different — but it is close enough that a React developer can be productive in aKt within an afternoon.

The execution model is LiveView's: a persistent WebSocket connection, server-side process per component instance, diffs sent over the wire. This is not a compromise. It is a strict upgrade for real-time UIs, collaborative tools, dashboards, and forms with server-side validation. For these applications, shipping zero JavaScript for your component logic is not a limitation; it is the correct architecture.

---

### Principle 2: The Single-File Component Is the Right Unit

LiveView's separation of `MyComponent.ex` and `my_component.html.heex` is reasonable for MVC developers. But React developers spent years arguing that separation of concerns does not mean separation of files. A button component's markup, behavior, and style are all concerns of the button. They belong together.

The `.akt` file is KorE's answer. One file, logic and markup. The template is not the whole file — it is a section of the file, just as the `return` statement is a section of a React function component. This is the `.tsx` model, not the `.heex` model.

---

### Principle 3: What Translates from Next.js

| Next.js concept | aKt equivalent |
|---|---|
| File-based routing | `pages/users/[id].akt` → `/users/:id` |
| Server Components | The default. Every component is server-side. |
| Client Components | `use client` at top of file — JS island |
| Layouts | `_layout.akt` in any directory |
| Loading states | `_loading.akt` |
| Error boundaries | `_error.akt` |
| `getServerSideProps` | `suspend fun loadData(props, session)` |
| SSR | Everything, always |

---

### Principle 4: What Does Not Translate

- **No Node.js.** aKt runs on the BEAM.
- **No hydration bundle.** Server components produce zero client JavaScript. There is no rehydration step.
- **No Virtual DOM.** The server maintains component state and a compiled render function. Diffs are computed from the template structure, not from comparing two in-memory trees.
- **No `useEffect` for data fetching.** Data fetching happens in `mount` or `loadData`, which are server-side functions.
- **No Redux/Zustand.** PubSub and process registries are the global state mechanism.

---

### Principle 5: The Diff Protocol as the Core Abstraction

A template like:

```
<div class="user-card">
  <h2>{ user.name }</h2>
  <p>{ user.email }</p>
</div>
```

has static parts (`<div class="user-card"><h2>`, `</h2><p>`, `</p></div>`) and dynamic parts (`user.name`, `user.email`). The compiler identifies this split at compile time. Static parts are sent to the client once, assigned numeric identifiers. Subsequently, only dynamic values are transmitted. A state change that updates `user.name` sends `{0: "Jane Doe"}` over the WebSocket — not the entire HTML.

This is what "no Virtual DOM" means in practice: the diff is derived from the structure of the compiled template, which the compiler has already analyzed.

---

## 11.2 — The `.akt` File Format

### The Structure

A `.akt` file contains two logical sections:

1. **Logic section**: Imports, type declarations, props, state, lifecycle functions, event handlers. Valid KorE code.
2. **Template section**: Markup with embedded KorE expressions.

The central design question is: how does the file indicate where the logic ends and the template begins?

---

### Option A: `template { }` Block

```kotlin
// UserCard.akt
import kore.akt.*

@Component
props UserCardProps {
    val user: User
    val showEmail: Boolean = true
}

fun formatName(user: User): String = "${user.firstName} ${user.lastName}"

template {
    <div class="user-card">
        <h2>{ formatName(props.user) }</h2>
        { if (props.showEmail) {
            <p class="email">{ props.user.email }</p>
        } }
    </div>
}
```

**Tradeoffs:** Unambiguous, familiar to Vue developers. Cost: verbosity, the `{ }` wrapping a template is confusing when `{ }` also means "KorE expression" inside the template, and the block semantics differ from a function body.

---

### Option B: `---` Separator (Astro/Svelte Style)

```kotlin
// UserCard.akt
import kore.akt.*

@Component
props UserCardProps {
    val user: User
    val showEmail: Boolean = true
}

fun formatName(user: User): String = "${user.firstName} ${user.lastName}"

---

<div class="user-card">
    <h2>{ formatName(props.user) }</h2>
    { if (props.showEmail) {
        <p class="email">{ props.user.email }</p>
    } }
</div>
```

**Tradeoffs:** Visually clean. Reads "here is the code, here is the output." Fragile if `---` appears in a multiline string in the logic section (the compiler handles this by requiring the `---` line to have no surrounding context), and the template runs to EOF which is slightly asymmetric. Split point is a context-free token any parser can find quickly.

---

### Option C: `render()` Function (JSX Style)

```kotlin
fun render(props: UserCardProps): AktNode {
    return (
        <div class="user-card">
            <h2>{ formatName(props.user) }</h2>
        </div>
    )
}
```

**Tradeoffs:** Most consistent with KorE syntax — the template is just code. No special file format. Cost: blurs the boundary between markup and logic. For stateful components, `render()` needs access to state somehow (implicit receiver or parameter). The parser must recognize `(` followed by `<` as the start of markup — a context-sensitive rule.

---

### Recommendation: Option B (`---` Separator), with `template { }` retained for multi-template files

The `---` separator is the right default. Clean, unambiguous for the common case, familiar to Astro/Svelte developers. `template { }` blocks are retained for components that need to declare multiple named templates (e.g., a `template(name = "loading")` variant).

The `render()` approach is rejected: it makes the logic/markup boundary a matter of convention rather than syntax.

**The canonical `.akt` file:**

```kotlin
// Counter.akt

import kore.akt.*
import kore.akt.live.*

props CounterProps {
    val initialCount: Int = 0
    val step: Int = 1
    val label: String = "Count"
}

data class CounterState(
    val count: Int,
    val lastUpdated: Instant?
)

fun mount(props: CounterProps): CounterState =
    CounterState(count = props.initialCount, lastUpdated = null)

fun handleIncrement(state: CounterState, props: CounterProps): CounterState =
    state.copy(count = state.count + props.step, lastUpdated = Instant.now())

fun handleDecrement(state: CounterState, props: CounterProps): CounterState =
    state.copy(count = state.count - props.step, lastUpdated = Instant.now())

fun handleReset(state: CounterState): CounterState =
    state.copy(count = 0, lastUpdated = null)

---

<div class="counter" role="region" aria-label={props.label}>
    <h3>{ props.label }: { state.count }</h3>
    <div class="controls">
        <button onClick={handleDecrement} aria-label="Decrease count">−</button>
        <button onClick={handleReset} aria-label="Reset count">Reset</button>
        <button onClick={handleIncrement} aria-label="Increase count">+</button>
    </div>
    { if (state.lastUpdated != null) {
        <p class="timestamp">Last updated: { state.lastUpdated.format("HH:mm:ss") }</p>
    } }
</div>
```

---

### The Markup Language

**HTML elements:** Standard HTML, self-closing with `/>`. `class` attributes accept static strings or expressions. No special class-binding syntax needed.

**KorE expressions:** Embedded with `{ }` (single braces, like JSX). Any KorE expression evaluating to a renderable value:

```kotlin
---
<div>
    <p>Hello, { user.name }!</p>
    <p>{ formatDate(order.createdAt) }</p>
    <span class={ when { state.isActive -> "active"; else -> "inactive" } }>Status</span>
    <Avatar user={user} size={.lg} />
</div>
```

**Component invocations:** PascalCase tags. The compiler distinguishes `<div>` (HTML, lowercase) from `<UserCard>` (component, uppercase).

**Conditional rendering — three forms:**

```kotlin
---
// Form 1: directive (recommended for multi-line blocks)
<div>
    {if state.isLoggedIn}
        <UserMenu user={state.user} />
    {else if state.isLoading}
        <LoadingSpinner />
    {else}
        <LoginButton />
    {/if}
</div>

// Form 2: inline expression
<div>
    { if (state.isLoggedIn) <UserMenu user={state.user} /> else null }
</div>

// Form 3: when expression (recommended for multi-branch value switching)
<div>
    { when (state.status) {
        .loading -> <LoadingSpinner />
        .error   -> <ErrorMessage message={state.error} />
        .ready   -> <UserMenu user={state.user} />
    } }
</div>
```

**List rendering — two forms:**

```kotlin
---
// Form 1: directive (recommended for block-level)
<ul>
    {for user in state.users}
        <li key={user.id}><UserCard user={user} /></li>
    {/for}
</ul>

// Form 2: pipeline (recommended when transforming)
<ul>
    { state.users
        |> filter { it.isActive }
        |> sortBy { it.name }
        |> map { user -> <li key={user.id}>{ user.name }</li> }
    }
</ul>
```

`key` is required on list children. Missing `key` → compiler warning. `key` must be a `String` expression.

**Attribute binding:**

```kotlin
---
<input
    type="text"
    value={state.inputValue}
    class={"form-input " + if (state.hasError) "error" else ""}
    disabled={state.isSubmitting}
    aria-invalid={state.hasError}
    aria-describedby={ if (state.hasError) "error-msg" else null }
/>
```

A `null` expression in an attribute position omits the attribute entirely. Boolean attributes: `disabled={true}` renders as `disabled`; `disabled={false}` omits it.

**Event binding:**

```kotlin
fun handleClick(event: ClickEvent, state: CounterState): CounterState =
    state.copy(count = state.count + 1)

fun handleInput(event: InputEvent, state: FormState): FormState =
    state.copy(value = event.value)

---
<div>
    <button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
    <button onClick={ { _ -> state.copy(count = 0) } }>Reset</button>
    <input type="text" value={state.value} onChange={handleInput} onBlur={handleBlur} />
    <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>...</form>
</div>
```

Handler signatures (compiler-verified):
```kotlin
fun handler(event: EventType, state: S): S
fun handler(state: S): S
fun handler(event: EventType, state: S): Pair<S, List<Command>>
fun handler(event: EventType, state: S, props: P): S
```

**Slots and children:**

```kotlin
// Card.akt — default children
props CardProps { val title: String }

---
<div class="card">
    <div class="card-header"><h3>{ props.title }</h3></div>
    <div class="card-body">{ children }</div>
</div>
```

Usage:
```kotlin
---
<Card title="User Profile">
    <UserAvatar user={user} />
    <UserDetails user={user} />
</Card>
```

Named slots:
```kotlin
// AppLayout.akt
---
<div class="app-layout">
    <nav>{ slot("nav") ?: <DefaultNav /> }</nav>
    <main>{ children }</main>
    <footer>{ slot("footer") ?: <DefaultFooter /> }</footer>
</div>
```

Usage:
```kotlin
---
<AppLayout>
    <slot name="nav"><CustomNav /></slot>
    <slot name="footer"><ArticleFooter /></slot>
    <ArticlePage article={state.article} />
</AppLayout>
```

Scoped slots — data from component back to caller:
```kotlin
// DataTable.akt
props DataTableProps<T> { val rows: List<T>; val rowKey: (T) -> String }

---
<table>
    <tbody>
        {for row in props.rows}
            <tr key={props.rowKey(row)}>{ slot("row", row) }</tr>
        {/for}
    </tbody>
</table>
```

Usage:
```kotlin
---
<DataTable rows={state.users} rowKey={ u -> u.id }>
    <slot name="row" let:row>
        <td>{ row.name }</td>
        <td>{ row.email }</td>
    </slot>
</DataTable>
```

**Fragments:** `<>...</>` for multiple root elements with no wrapper.

**Comments:** `{/* ... */}` = compile-time only, not rendered. `<!-- -->` = rendered to client HTML.

---

### `.akt` Compilation Phases

**Phase 1:** Find `---` line. Split. Error if missing.

**Phase 2:** Parse logic section as normal KorE. Collect props type, state type, function declarations.

**Phase 3:** Parse template section with the aKt template parser. Produces `TemplateAST`.

**Phase 4:** Type-check template. Scope = `{ props, state, all top-level functions }`. Verify every `{ expr }` is renderable, every component invocation matches its props type, every event handler matches its expected signature.

**Phase 5:** Static/dynamic split. Classify every node. Extract static subtrees as binary constants.

**Phase 6:** Code generation. Emit Erlang Abstract Format. For `@LiveComponent`: GenServer module + render function + handle_event dispatch + handle_info dispatch.

**Generated BEAM modules for `pages/users/[id]/Profile.akt`:**

```
'KorE.Pages.Users.Id.Profile'         — the GenServer
'KorE.Pages.Users.Id.Profile.Render'  — render functions (separated for testability)
'KorE.Pages.Users.Id.Profile.Props'   — props type module
```

---

## 11.3 — The Component Model

### Stateless Function Components (`@Component`)

No state, no lifecycle, no process. The compiler generates a single BEAM module with a `render/1` function. Zero process overhead.

```kotlin
// UserCard.akt
import kore.akt.*
import myapp.domain.User

@Component
props UserCardProps {
    val user: User
    val size: AvatarSize = .medium
    val showRole: Boolean = false
    val onClick: ((User) -> Unit)? = null
}

---

<div
    class={"user-card user-card--${props.size.name}"}
    role={ if (props.onClick != null) "button" else null }
    tabIndex={ if (props.onClick != null) 0 else null }
    onClick={ if (props.onClick != null) { _ -> props.onClick!!(props.user) } else null }
>
    <Avatar src={props.user.avatarUrl} alt={props.user.name} size={props.size} />
    <div class="user-card__info">
        <span class="user-card__name">{ props.user.name }</span>
        { if (props.showRole) {
            <span class="user-card__role">{ props.user.role.displayName }</span>
        } }
    </div>
</div>
```

**Inline component declarations** (multiple small components in one file):

```kotlin
// badges.akt
@Component
props BadgeProps { val label: String; val variant: BadgeVariant = .default }

component Badge {
    <span class={"badge badge--${props.variant.name}"}>{ props.label }</span>
}

@Component
props StatusDotProps { val online: Boolean }

component StatusDot {
    <span
        class={"status-dot " + if (props.online) "status-dot--online" else "status-dot--offline"}
        aria-label={ if (props.online) "Online" else "Offline" }
    />
}
```

Inline `component` declarations use a block body instead of `---`.

---

### Stateful Server Components (`@LiveComponent`)

Each mounted instance = one GenServer process. The process holds component state. When state changes, the process re-runs the render function and sends the diff to the client.

```kotlin
// LiveSearch.akt
import kore.akt.*
import kore.akt.live.*
import myapp.services.SearchService

@LiveComponent
props LiveSearchProps {
    val placeholder: String = "Search..."
    val minLength: Int = 2
    val onSelect: ((SearchResult) -> Unit)? = null
}

data class LiveSearchState(
    val query: String = "",
    val results: List<SearchResult> = emptyList(),
    val loading: Boolean = false,
    val selected: SearchResult? = null
)

fun mount(props: LiveSearchProps): LiveSearchState = LiveSearchState()

fun handleQueryChange(event: InputEvent, state: LiveSearchState, props: LiveSearchProps): Pair<LiveSearchState, List<Command>> {
    val newQuery = event.value
    return if (newQuery.length >= props.minLength) {
        Pair(
            state.copy(query = newQuery, loading = true, results = emptyList()),
            listOf(Command.async("search") { SearchService.search(newQuery) })
        )
    } else {
        Pair(state.copy(query = newQuery, results = emptyList(), loading = false), emptyList())
    }
}

fun handleSearchResult(results: List<SearchResult>, state: LiveSearchState): LiveSearchState =
    state.copy(results = results, loading = false)

fun handleSelect(result: SearchResult, state: LiveSearchState, props: LiveSearchProps): Pair<LiveSearchState, List<Command>> {
    val commands = if (props.onSelect != null) {
        listOf(Command.callParent(props.onSelect!!, result))
    } else emptyList()
    return Pair(state.copy(selected = result, query = result.title, results = emptyList()), commands)
}

---

<div class="live-search" role="combobox" aria-expanded={state.results.isNotEmpty()}>
    <input
        type="text"
        value={state.query}
        placeholder={props.placeholder}
        onChange={handleQueryChange}
        aria-autocomplete="list"
        aria-controls="search-results"
    />
    { if (state.loading) {
        <div class="live-search__spinner" role="status" aria-label="Searching..." />
    } }
    { if (state.results.isNotEmpty()) {
        <ul id="search-results" class="live-search__results" role="listbox">
            {for result in state.results}
                <li
                    key={result.id}
                    class={"live-search__result" + if (result == state.selected) " live-search__result--selected" else ""}
                    role="option"
                    aria-selected={result == state.selected}
                    onClick={ { _ -> handleSelect(result, state, props) } }
                >
                    { result.title }
                    { if (result.subtitle != null) {
                        <span class="live-search__subtitle">{ result.subtitle }</span>
                    } }
                </li>
            {/for}
        </ul>
    } }
</div>
```

---

### Props System

```kotlin
props MyComponentProps {
    val requiredString: String              // Required
    val requiredUser: User                  // Required
    val optionalInt: Int = 0                // Optional with default
    val optionalText: String? = null        // Optional nullable
    val callback: ((Event) -> Unit)? = null // Optional callback
}
```

Prop validation is compile-time. Passing wrong type → compile error. Missing required prop → compile error. Unknown prop → compile error.

**Prop spreading:**
```kotlin
props ButtonProps { val label: String; val variant: ButtonVariant = .primary; val onClick: () -> Unit }

---
<div class="button-wrapper">
    <Button ...{props} />
</div>
```

**Computed prop defaults:**
```kotlin
props AvatarProps {
    val user: User
    val alt: String by { props.user.name }  // Computed from other prop
    val size: Int = 40
}
```

---

### Component Composition

Stateless components compose by nesting: outer render evaluates inner render function, splices result.

Stateful components compose as **process composition**: each `@LiveComponent` in the tree is an independent GenServer. The parent sends props to the child process; the child runs its own render cycle and sends its own diffs. Diffs are merged by the client runtime.

```kotlin
// Parent to child: via props (normal)
<ChildComponent value={state.someValue} />

// Child to parent: via callback prop
fun handleChildEvent(result: ChildResult, state: ParentState): ParentState =
    state.copy(childResult = result)

// In template:
<ChildComponent onResult={handleChildEvent} />
```

---

## 11.4 — State and Lifecycle

### `useState` → Component State

React: multiple independent `useState` calls.

aKt: one typed `data class` state record, initialized in `mount`, updated by returning new value from handlers.

```kotlin
data class MyState(val count: Int = 0, val user: User? = null)

fun mount(props: MyProps): MyState = MyState(count = props.initialCount)

fun handleIncrement(state: MyState): MyState = state.copy(count = state.count + 1)
fun handleSetUser(user: User, state: MyState): MyState = state.copy(user = user)
```

If managing multiple independent pieces of state feels cumbersome, that is a signal to split the component.

---

### `useEffect(() => {}, [])` → `mount`

```kotlin
fun mount(props: DashboardProps): Pair<DashboardState, List<Command>> {
    return Pair(
        DashboardState(),
        listOf(
            Command.run { Analytics.track(.pageView, mapOf("page" to "dashboard")) },
            Command.subscribe("updates:${props.userId}")
        )
    )
}
```

When `mount` needs side effects, return `Pair<State, List<Command>>`. When it needs no side effects, return `State` directly.

---

### `useEffect(() => {}, [dep])` → `update`

```kotlin
fun update(newProps: PostListProps, oldProps: PostListProps, state: PostListState): Pair<PostListState, List<Command>> {
    return if (newProps.userId != oldProps.userId) {
        Pair(
            state.copy(posts = emptyList(), loading = true),
            listOf(Command.async("fetch_posts") { PostService.getUserPosts(newProps.userId) })
        )
    } else {
        Pair(state, emptyList())
    }
}
```

There is no reactive dependency tracking. If the "dependency" is an internal state value rather than a prop, trigger the effect directly from the state transition that changes the value.

---

### `useEffect(() => { return cleanup }, [])` → `terminate`

```kotlin
fun mount(props: FeedProps): Pair<FeedState, List<Command>> =
    Pair(FeedState(), listOf(Command.subscribe("feed:${props.userId}")))

fun terminate(state: FeedState, props: FeedProps): Unit {
    ConnectionPool.release(state.connection)  // Explicit cleanup for non-Command resources
}
```

`Command.subscribe` automatically unsubscribes on terminate. Explicit `terminate` is needed only for resources outside of `Command` lifecycle management.

---

### `useReducer` → Explicit State Machine

`useReducer` is not needed as a distinct construct. Event handler functions collectively ARE the reducer. For complex state machines:

```kotlin
sealed class CounterEvent {
    object Increment : CounterEvent()
    object Decrement : CounterEvent()
    data class Reset(val to: Int = 0) : CounterEvent()
}

data class CounterState(val count: Int, val step: Int = 1)

fun reduce(event: CounterEvent, state: CounterState): CounterState = when (event) {
    is CounterEvent.Increment -> state.copy(count = state.count + state.step)
    is CounterEvent.Decrement -> state.copy(count = state.count - state.step)
    is CounterEvent.Reset     -> state.copy(count = event.to)
}

fun handleIncrement(state: CounterState) = reduce(CounterEvent.Increment, state)
fun handleDecrement(state: CounterState) = reduce(CounterEvent.Decrement, state)
```

---

### `useContext` → PubSub and Process Registry

For application-wide global state:

```kotlin
fun mount(props: ThemedComponentProps): Pair<ThemedState, List<Command>> =
    Pair(
        ThemedState(theme = ThemeRegistry.current()),
        listOf(Command.subscribe("theme:changes"))
    )

fun handle_info(msg: ThemeChanged, state: ThemedState): ThemedState =
    state.copy(theme = msg.newTheme)
```

For per-session data (current user, locale): passed through the router as session context, accessible in `mount`:

```kotlin
fun mount(props: MyProps, session: Session): Pair<MyState, List<Command>> {
    val currentUser = session.get<User>("current_user")
    return Pair(MyState(currentUser = currentUser), emptyList())
}
```

---

### `useRef` → JS Hook Handle

For DOM imperatives (focus, scroll), use the `use:` directive:

```kotlin
---
<input
    type="text"
    use:focus={state.shouldFocus}  // JS hook triggers focus when true
    value={state.value}
    onChange={handleChange}
/>
```

For storing server-side mutable references across renders, store in state — unlike React, state fields not referenced in the template do not trigger diff work.

---

### `useMemo` / `useCallback` → Not Needed

`useMemo` is unnecessary on the BEAM. There is no Virtual DOM reconciliation to prevent. The diff protocol only sends changed dynamic values. Functions in the template are pure KorE functions called on every render; this is correct and cheap.

```kotlin
// No useMemo needed
fun sortedUsers(state: UserListState): List<User> = state.users.sortedBy { it.name }

---
<ul>
    {for user in sortedUsers(state)}
        <li key={user.id}>{ user.name }</li>
    {/for}
</ul>
```

If a computation is genuinely expensive, store the result in state and update it only when the source changes:

```kotlin
fun handleUsersLoaded(users: List<User>, state: UserListState): UserListState =
    state.copy(
        users = users,
        sortedUsers = users.sortedBy { it.name }
    )
```

---

### `useTransition` → `Command.async`

```kotlin
fun handleTabChange(tab: Tab, state: PageState): Pair<PageState, List<Command>> =
    Pair(
        state.copy(activeTab = tab, loading = true),
        listOf(Command.async("load_tab_data") { TabService.loadData(tab) })
    )

fun handleTabDataLoaded(result: Ok<TabData>, state: PageState): PageState =
    state.copy(tabData = result.value, loading = false)
```

---

### Complete Lifecycle Diagram

```
Client connects
      │
      ▼
  loadData(params, session)    ← Page-level data loading (like getServerSideProps)
      │
      ▼
  mount(props)                 ← GenServer starts, initial state set, Commands dispatched
      │
      ▼
  render(state)                ← Template evaluated, Rendered diff tree produced
      │                        ← Initial HTML sent to client
      ▼
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                    Component Running                        │
  │                                                             │
  │  User event   → handle_event → new state → render → diff   │
  │  Async result → handle_info  → new state → render → diff   │
  │  PubSub msg   → handle_info  → new state → render → diff   │
  │  Props change → update       → new state → render → diff   │
  │                                                             │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
      │
      ▼
  terminate(state)             ← Client disconnects or navigates, cleanup runs
```

**Complete lifecycle example:**

```kotlin
// RealtimeFeed.akt
import kore.akt.*
import kore.akt.live.*
import myapp.services.{PostService}
import myapp.domain.{Post}

@LiveComponent
props RealtimeFeedProps {
    val userId: String
    val initialLimit: Int = 20
}

data class FeedState(
    val posts: List<Post> = emptyList(),
    val loading: Boolean = true,
    val error: String? = null,
    val newPostCount: Int = 0,
    val limit: Int = 20
)

fun mount(props: RealtimeFeedProps): Pair<FeedState, List<Command>> =
    Pair(
        FeedState(limit = props.initialLimit),
        listOf(
            Command.async("load_posts") { PostService.getRecent(props.userId, props.initialLimit) },
            Command.subscribe("feed:${props.userId}")
        )
    )

fun handle_info(msg: AsyncResult<"load_posts", List<Post>>, state: FeedState): FeedState =
    when (msg) {
        is Ok -> state.copy(posts = msg.value, loading = false)
        is Err -> state.copy(error = msg.reason.toString(), loading = false)
    }

fun handle_info(msg: NewPost, state: FeedState): FeedState =
    state.copy(newPostCount = state.newPostCount + 1)

fun update(newProps: RealtimeFeedProps, oldProps: RealtimeFeedProps, state: FeedState): Pair<FeedState, List<Command>> =
    if (newProps.userId != oldProps.userId) {
        Pair(
            FeedState(loading = true, limit = newProps.initialLimit),
            listOf(
                Command.unsubscribe("feed:${oldProps.userId}"),
                Command.async("load_posts") { PostService.getRecent(newProps.userId, newProps.initialLimit) },
                Command.subscribe("feed:${newProps.userId}")
            )
        )
    } else Pair(state, emptyList())

fun terminate(state: FeedState, props: RealtimeFeedProps): Unit {
    PostService.recordLastViewed(props.userId, state.posts.firstOrNull()?.id)
}

fun handleLoadNew(state: FeedState, props: RealtimeFeedProps): Pair<FeedState, List<Command>> =
    Pair(
        state.copy(loading = true, newPostCount = 0),
        listOf(Command.async("load_posts") { PostService.getRecent(props.userId, state.limit) })
    )

---

<div class="feed">
    { if (state.newPostCount > 0) {
        <button class="feed__new-posts-banner" onClick={handleLoadNew}>
            { state.newPostCount } new { if (state.newPostCount == 1) "post" else "posts" } — click to load
        </button>
    } }

    { when {
        state.loading && state.posts.isEmpty() -> <FeedSkeleton />
        state.error != null -> (
            <div class="feed__error" role="alert">
                <p>Failed to load posts: { state.error }</p>
                <button onClick={handleLoadNew}>Retry</button>
            </div>
        )
        state.posts.isEmpty() -> <EmptyFeed userId={props.userId} />
        else -> (
            <>
                <ul class="feed__list">
                    {for post in state.posts}
                        <li key={post.id}><PostCard post={post} /></li>
                    {/for}
                </ul>
                <button class="feed__load-more" onClick={handleLoadNew} disabled={state.loading}>
                    { if (state.loading) "Loading..." else "Load more" }
                </button>
            </>
        )
    } }
</div>
```

---

## 11.5 — Event Handling

### The Round-Trip Model

User clicks → aKt JS runtime captures event → WebSocket message sent → component GenServer receives → handler called → new state → render + diff → diff sent → DOM updated.

The round trip typically completes in under 50ms on a co-located server.

---

### Standard Events

| aKt attribute | DOM event | Payload type |
|---|---|---|
| `onClick` | `click` | `ClickEvent` |
| `onChange` | `change` | `ChangeEvent` |
| `onInput` | `input` | `InputEvent` |
| `onSubmit` | `submit` | `SubmitEvent` |
| `onKeyDown` | `keydown` | `KeyboardEvent` |
| `onKeyUp` | `keyup` | `KeyboardEvent` |
| `onFocus` | `focus` | `FocusEvent` |
| `onBlur` | `blur` | `FocusEvent` |
| `onMouseEnter` | `mouseenter` | `MouseEvent` |
| `onMouseLeave` | `mouseleave` | `MouseEvent` |
| `onDragStart` | `dragstart` | `DragEvent` |
| `onDrop` | `drop` | `DragEvent` |
| `onScroll` | `scroll` | `ScrollEvent` |

**Full round-trip for `onClick`:**

1. aKt JS runtime detects `click` event
2. Reads `phx-click="handleAddItem"` attribute from element
3. Sends `{"type": "event", "name": "handleAddItem", "payload": {}}` over WebSocket
4. GenServer dispatches to `handleAddItem`
5. Handler returns `(newState, [Command.run(...)])`
6. GenServer updates state, executes commands, runs `render(newState)`, diffs against previous render
7. Diff sent to client
8. aKt JS runtime applies patch to DOM

---

### Event Payload Types

```kotlin
data class ClickEvent(val target: ElementRef, val clientX: Int, val clientY: Int, val button: Int,
    val ctrlKey: Boolean, val shiftKey: Boolean, val altKey: Boolean, val metaKey: Boolean)

data class InputEvent(val value: String, val target: ElementRef)

data class ChangeEvent(val value: String, val checked: Boolean?, val files: List<FileRef>?, val target: ElementRef)

data class KeyboardEvent(val key: String, val code: String,
    val ctrlKey: Boolean, val shiftKey: Boolean, val altKey: Boolean, val metaKey: Boolean, val repeat: Boolean)

data class SubmitEvent(val formData: Map<String, String>, val target: ElementRef)

data class FocusEvent(val target: ElementRef, val relatedTarget: ElementRef?)

data class MouseEvent(val clientX: Int, val clientY: Int, val target: ElementRef)
```

---

### Preventing Default

```kotlin
---
<form onSubmit={handleSubmit} prevent:submit>...</form>
<a href="/dashboard" onClick={handleNavClick} prevent:click>Dashboard</a>
```

`prevent:` is a client-side instruction: call `event.preventDefault()` before sending over WebSocket. Necessary because form submission and link navigation would navigate away before the server responds.

Navigate programmatically:
```kotlin
fun handleSubmit(event: SubmitEvent, state: FormState): Pair<FormState, List<Command>> {
    val errors = validate(event.formData)
    return if (errors.isEmpty()) {
        Pair(state, listOf(Command.navigate("/dashboard")))
    } else {
        Pair(state.copy(errors = errors), emptyList())
    }
}
```

---

### Debouncing and Throttling

```kotlin
---
// Debounce: wait 300ms after last keystroke before sending
<input type="search" value={state.query} onInput={handleSearch} debounce:input={300} />

// Throttle: send at most once per 200ms
<div onMouseMove={handleMouseMove} throttle:mousemove={200} />
```

Both are client-side: the aKt JS runtime buffers events before sending over WebSocket.

---

### JS Hooks for Client-Side Behavior

For canvas, animations, third-party JS libraries:

```kotlin
---
<canvas use:Chart data-config={Json.encode(chartConfig)} width="800" height="400" />
```

```javascript
// In app.js
AktRuntime.start({
    hooks: {
        Chart: {
            mounted() {
                const config = JSON.parse(this.el.dataset.config)
                this.chart = new Chart(this.el, config)
            },
            updated() {
                const config = JSON.parse(this.el.dataset.config)
                this.chart.data = config.data
                this.chart.update()
            },
            destroyed() { this.chart.destroy() },
            handleEvent(event) {
                if (event.type === "highlight") this.chart.highlight(event.dataIndex)
            }
        }
    }
})
```

`this` context: `this.el` (DOM element), `this.pushEvent(name, payload)` (→ server), `this.handleEvent(name, callback)` (← server), `this.pushEventTo(selector, name, payload)`.

---

### Optimistic Updates

```kotlin
data class LikeButtonState(val liked: Boolean, val likeCount: Int, val pending: Boolean = false)

fun handleLike(state: LikeButtonState, props: LikeButtonProps): Pair<LikeButtonState, List<Command>> {
    // Optimistic: immediately reflect the change
    val optimisticState = state.copy(
        liked = !state.liked,
        likeCount = if (state.liked) state.likeCount - 1 else state.likeCount + 1,
        pending = true
    )
    return Pair(
        optimisticState,
        listOf(Command.async("toggle_like") { LikeService.toggle(props.postId) })
    )
}

fun handle_info(msg: AsyncResult<"toggle_like", LikeResult>, state: LikeButtonState): LikeButtonState =
    when (msg) {
        is Ok -> state.copy(liked = msg.value.liked, likeCount = msg.value.count, pending = false)
        is Err -> state.copy(  // Revert on error
            liked = !state.liked,
            likeCount = if (state.liked) state.likeCount + 1 else state.likeCount - 1,
            pending = false
        )
    }
```

---

### Complete Form Example

```kotlin
// ContactForm.akt
import kore.akt.*
import kore.akt.live.*
import myapp.services.MailService

@LiveComponent
props ContactFormProps { val onSuccess: (() -> Unit)? = null }

data class FormValues(val name: String = "", val email: String = "",
    val subject: String = "", val message: String = "")

data class ContactFormState(
    val values: FormValues = FormValues(),
    val errors: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(),
    val submitting: Boolean = false,
    val submitted: Boolean = false,
    val serverError: String? = null
)

fun mount(props: ContactFormProps): ContactFormState = ContactFormState()

fun handleFieldChange(event: InputEvent, state: ContactFormState): ContactFormState {
    val fieldName = event.target.name
    val newValues = when (fieldName) {
        "name"    -> state.values.copy(name = event.value)
        "email"   -> state.values.copy(email = event.value)
        "subject" -> state.values.copy(subject = event.value)
        "message" -> state.values.copy(message = event.value)
        else      -> state.values
    }
    return state.copy(values = newValues, errors = state.errors - fieldName)
}

fun handleSubmit(event: SubmitEvent, state: ContactFormState): Pair<ContactFormState, List<Command>> {
    val allErrors = validateAll(state.values)
    return if (allErrors.isNotEmpty()) {
        Pair(state.copy(errors = allErrors), emptyList())
    } else {
        Pair(
            state.copy(submitting = true, serverError = null),
            listOf(Command.async("send_message") { MailService.send(state.values) })
        )
    }
}

fun handle_info(msg: AsyncResult<"send_message", Unit>, state: ContactFormState): Pair<ContactFormState, List<Command>> =
    when (msg) {
        is Ok -> Pair(state.copy(submitted = true, submitting = false), emptyList())
        is Err -> Pair(state.copy(submitting = false, serverError = "Failed to send. Please try again."), emptyList())
    }

fun validateField(field: String, values: FormValues): String? = when (field) {
    "name"    -> if (values.name.isBlank()) "Name is required" else null
    "email"   -> if (!values.email.matches(Regex.email)) "Valid email required" else null
    "subject" -> if (values.subject.isBlank()) "Subject is required" else null
    "message" -> if (values.message.length < 10) "Message must be at least 10 characters" else null
    else      -> null
}

fun validateAll(values: FormValues): Map<String, String> =
    listOf("name", "email", "subject", "message")
        .mapNotNull { field -> validateField(field, values)?.let { field to it } }
        .toMap()

---

{ if (state.submitted) {
    <div class="contact-form__success" role="status">
        <h3>Message sent!</h3>
        <p>We'll get back to you within 24 hours.</p>
    </div>
} else {
    <form class="contact-form" onSubmit={handleSubmit} prevent:submit novalidate>
        { if (state.serverError != null) {
            <div class="contact-form__server-error" role="alert">{ state.serverError }</div>
        } }

        <div class={"form-field" + if (state.errors["name"] != null) " form-field--error" else ""}>
            <label for="name">Name *</label>
            <input id="name" name="name" type="text" value={state.values.name}
                onInput={handleFieldChange}
                aria-required="true"
                aria-invalid={state.errors["name"] != null}
                aria-describedby={ if (state.errors["name"] != null) "name-error" else null }
            />
            { if (state.errors["name"] != null) {
                <p id="name-error" class="form-field__error" role="alert">{ state.errors["name"] }</p>
            } }
        </div>

        {/* ...other fields follow same pattern... */}

        <button type="submit" class="btn btn--primary"
            disabled={state.submitting} aria-busy={state.submitting}>
            { if (state.submitting) "Sending..." else "Send Message" }
        </button>
    </form>
} }
```
